availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

Use for any Cloudflare development task. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.

availableCommands.name: cloudflare-email-service
availableCommands.description: Send and receive transactional emails with Cloudflare Email Service (Email Sending + Email Routing). Use when building email sending (Workers binding or REST API), email routing, Agents SDK email handling, or integrating email into any app — Workers, Node.js, Python, Go, etc. Also use for email deliverability, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, wrangler email setup, MCP email tools, or when a coding agent needs to send emails. Even for simple requests like "add email to my Worker" — this skill has critical config details.

availableCommands.name: cloudflare-one
availableCommands.description: Guides Cloudflare One Zero Trust and SASE work across Access, Gateway, WARP, Tunnel, Cloudflare WAN, DLP, CASB, device posture, and identity. Use when designing, configuring, troubleshooting, or reviewing Cloudflare One deployments. Retrieval-first: use current Cloudflare docs/API schemas instead of embedded product docs.

availableCommands.name: cloudflare-one-migrations
availableCommands.description: Plans migrations from Zscaler ZIA/ZPA, Palo Alto, legacy VPN, SWG, or SASE stacks to Cloudflare One. Use for migration assessments, policy mapping, rollout plans, and parity/gap analysis.

availableCommands.name: durable-objects
availableCommands.description: Create and review Cloudflare Durable Objects. availableCommands.name: turnstile-spin

availableCommands.name: web-perf

Use when asked to audit, profile, debug, or optimize page load performance, Lighthouse scores, or site speed. Biases towards retrieval from current documentation over pre-trained knowledge.

<content>
# BusLink Studio: PRD (BMAD phase 2)

Inputs: `product-brief.md`, `research/00-owner-research-brief.pdf`, `research/01-competitors-and-features.md`, `research/02-standards-and-dashboard-design.md`, `research/03-platform-tauri-android-usb.md`.
Status: approved scope "plus-control" (owner, 2026-11-11). Each requirement has an ID that the Kiro spec cites.

## 1. Goals and non-goals
**Goals:** one Modbus workbench on Windows, Android (USB OTG) and a LAN browser view, sharing one profile format. Data quality and data age are always visible. Writes are safe. Judges can try everything with a simulator.

**Non-goals (competition):**
- Cloud accounts, payments, Play Store publishing.
- Driving a real VFD or heater (simulator profiles only).
- Writes from the LAN browser.
- Linux/macOS builds. Tauri supports them, but they are untested here.

## 2. Users and top jobs
| User | Job | Pain it removes (research/01) |
|---|---|---|
| Commissioning technician | Connect a new device, find the right registers, check the values, hand over a report | #1 addressing, #2 word order, #3 unknown serial settings, #4 wiring vs software |
| Maintenance in the field | Check a device on the plant floor with only a phone | #10 fragile Android apps; no shared profile between PC and phone |
| Supervisor / trainer | Watch live values on any screen; run a lab without hardware | #9 stale values look healthy; labs need a simulator |
| Integrator | Change unit ID/baud or a setpoint safely, with a record | #7 unsafe writes |

## 3. Functional requirements
### Connectivity
- **R1 RTU desktop:** Windows COM ports. Detect WCH adapters by VID:PID (CH343 1A86:55D3 as inbox CDC-ACM, CH340 1A86:7523, CH9102 1A86:55D4), not by friendly name. Baud 300–3 000 000, data 7/8, parity N/E/O, stop 1/2.
- **R2 RTU Android:** USB OTG with a permission flow. Rotation keeps the session (state lives in the Rust core). A `connectedDevice` foreground service keeps polling with the screen off. Detach → DISCONNECTED, and nothing auto-resumes writes. Target API 36.
- **R3 Modbus TCP:** MBAP with transaction IDs, reconnect with backoff, unit ID. RTU-over-TCP is a separate transport type.
- **R4 One master per bus:** one scheduler queue per link. One failing device never blocks the others (backoff on it).

### Protocol and data
- **R5 Function codes:** FC01/02/03/04 read; FC05/06/15/16 write. Spec limits: 125 registers (FC03/04), 2000 coils, 123 registers (FC16). Merge contiguous reads into blocks.
- **R6 Codec:** U16/I16/U32/I32/U64/I64/F32/F64, bit fields, string. Word/byte order ABCD/CDAB/BADC/DCBA, stored explicitly in the profile. Scale, offset, unit, decimals, valid range, sentinel values.
- **R7 Quality:** every sample carries GOOD / TIMEOUT / CRC_ERROR / EXCEPTION(code) / STALE / DECODE_ERROR / DISCONNECTED, plus `age_ms`, source timestamp and receive timestamp. Last-good values are shown as stale, never as fresh. (OPC UA Good/Uncertain/Bad mapping per research/02.)
- **R8 Addressing:** always show the manual/documentation address *and* the PDU offset. Never send 40001-style numbers raw.

### Profiles
- **R9 Device profile:** JSON, versioned, schema-validated. Holds identity, serial defaults, register blocks, tags (address, FC, type, order, scale, unit, range, writable, min/max write), commands, and a support level: `generic | documented | simulated | hardware_verified` with source (manual and page). Profiles and device instances are separate.
- **R10 Bundled profiles:**
  - BGT-SMPS 8-in-1 soil sensor (`documented`, upgraded to `hardware_verified` after the real test).
  - Simulated VFD (`simulated`).
  - Simulated temperature controller (`simulated`).
  - Simulated energy meter (`simulated`).
  - A generic holding-register template.
- **R11 Import:** CSV/XLSX register map with preview and address-base detection. `.mbmap` read-only import (P2).

### UI
- **R12 Connection center:** ports/adapters, USB permission state, serial settings, TCP host, link statistics (TX/RX, CRC, timeouts, cycle time).
- **R13 Live dashboard:** ISA-101 high-performance style (grey base, color only for abnormal states, analog bar with normal range). Tiles show value, unit, quality text and age. Density toggle; Indonesian and English.
- **R14 Trends:** multiple tags with unit axes, cursor, zoom. **Gaps for lost communication, never interpolated.** Raw samples separate from display decimation (min-max). Alarm bands.
- **R15 Register inspector:** doc address, PDU offset, raw hex, decoded value in all four orders side by side, and the last request/response frame.
- **R16 Alarms (ISA-18.2):** threshold, hysteresis/deadband, on/off delay, priority, acknowledge, shelve with expiry. Communication alarms kept separate from process alarms. Alarm log.
- **R17 Commissioning wizard:** change unit ID or baud on one device, with journal → write → reconnect at the new settings → read-back → pass/fail. A recovery hint shows the old settings.
- **R18 Control panel (simulated VFD + temperature controller):**
  - The command service requires the device to be armed (session timeout), checks bounds, and asks for confirmation with an explicit label ("Apply setpoint 40.0 °C").
  - It encodes a frame preview, writes once (no automatic retry), reads back, and records the audit entry.
  - A software stop is always reachable and labeled "not an E-stop".
- **R19 Reports:** session summary (devices, profile versions, quality statistics, alarms, commands) exported as PDF/HTML.

### Data
- **R20 Historian:** SQLite WAL with tables sessions, devices, tags, samples, events, commands, outbox. Logging interval separate from polling interval. Retention setting.
- **R21 Export:** CSV (UTF-8, ISO-8601 UTC, quality and age columns, formula-injection guard), XLSX (Measurements, Devices, Configuration, Events, Commands sheets, numbers kept as numbers), JSON. Android saves through SAF.

### Sharing
- **R22 LAN dashboard:** opt-in. The app serves the same frontend (read-only routes + WebSocket stream) on a user-chosen interface/port, with a per-session token, TLS (self-signed per session; the URL/QR carries the token), and no write endpoints. Works from Windows and Android.
- **R23 MQTT telemetry:** opt-in. MQTT 5 over TLS, topic `buslink/{site}/{gateway}/{device}/{tag}` or a Sparkplug-B-compatible namespace (decision in architecture), payload with ts/seq/value/unit/quality/profile_version, a bounded offline outbox, deduplication by sequence. Credentials go in the OS secret store and never into project files.

### Training
- **R24 Simulator:** built-in multi-device RTU-over-loopback and TCP simulator with the bundled simulated profiles. Fault injection: timeout, CRC error, exception, stale, wrong word order. A **training mode** with guided exercises in Indonesian and English.

## 4. Non-functional requirements
- **N1 Safety:** read-only by default. Writes only through the command service. No broadcast writes. Audit trail for every command.
- **N2 Security:** IEC 62443-minded. LAN and MQTT off by default. Tokens + TLS. Profiles are data only (no scripts). No secrets in exports or logs. CSV formula guard.
- **N3 Performance (targets, to be measured):** UI keeps 60 fps with 50 tags at 1 Hz. Trend of 100k points renders in under 1 s on desktop. Android stays responsive at 10 tags/s.
- **N4 Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA. Status shown as text plus color. Keyboard operation on desktop. Touch targets ≥ 24 CSS px (AA), with 44 px on primary mobile actions. Reduced motion.
- **N5 Packaging:** Windows NSIS installer (WebView2 bootstrapper) + portable exe. Android APK (arm64). SHA-256 sums.
- **N6 Evidence:** a separate pass/fail matrix for simulator and for hardware. A profile becomes `hardware_verified` only with recorded evidence.

## 5. Acceptance (demo)
1. Fresh Windows install → Training mode → read 3 simulated devices → trend shows a gap when a fault is injected → export XLSX with quality columns.
2. Real BGT-SMPS sensor through the CH343G adapter on Windows, then the same profile on the Samsung A35 via OTG. Values match within one poll.
3. Browser on the LAN shows the phone's live dashboard, read-only.
4. Simulated VFD: arm → set frequency 30.0 Hz → read-back OK → stop → audit log entry.
5. MQTT: messages arrive at a local broker with sequence numbers; disconnect → outbox → replay without duplicates.

</content>
</file>

# BusLink Studio: architecture (BMAD phase 3) Covers the PRD requirement IDs (R1–R24, N1–N6). Technical facts are from `research/03-platform-tauri-android-usb.md`. ## Context ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Device["Windows PC / Android phone (one Tauri 2 app)"] UI[Web UI
TypeScript + uPlot] -- Tauri IPC --> Svc[App services] Svc --> Core[buslink-core
codec · scheduler · profiles · quality · command service] Core --> Tr{Transport trait} Tr --> SerW[Serial: Windows COM] Tr --> SerA[Serial: Android USB OTG] Tr --> TCP[Modbus TCP] Tr --> Sim[buslink-sim
in-process simulator] Core --> Hist[(SQLite historian)] Core --> Bus[Sample bus
broadcast channel] Bus --> UI Bus --> LAN[axum LAN server
read-only + WS] Bus --> MQ[MQTT publisher
outbox] end SerW & SerA --> RS485[USB-RS485 CH343G → RS485 bus → devices] TCP --> PLC[Modbus TCP devices] LAN --> Browser[LAN browser] MQ --> Broker[MQTT broker] ``` ## Repository layout ``` crates/buslink-core/ # protocol (RTU/TCP framing, CRC), codec, profile schema + validation, # scheduler (one queue per link), quality, alarms, command service, historian, export crates/buslink-sim/ # deterministic simulator: soil sensor, VFD, temperature controller, energy meter; fault injection src-tauri/ # Tauri shell: IPC commands, transports (Windows serial, Android USB), LAN server, MQTT src-tauri/gen/android/ # generated Android project + Kotlin USB permission / FGS src/ # web UI (TypeScript, Vite), shared by the desktop window, Android WebView and LAN browsers profiles/ # bundled device profiles (JSON) + schema video/ # Remotion demo video project docs/ # BMAD, design, verification, Kiro evidence ``` ## Key decisions | # | Decision | Alternatives | Why | |---|---|---|---| | D1 | **Own RTU/TCP framing in `buslink-core`**, reusing `rmodbus`-style pure codec ideas; no async transport crate in core | tokio-modbus | Core stays sync and testable with a fake transport (property tests on CRC/framing). Length-based RTU parsing (from FC and byte count) is robust against USB fragmentation on Android (research/03 risk table). | | D2 | **Transport trait** `open/configure/read(timeout)/write/flush/close` + detach event; implementations for Windows serial (`serialport`), Android USB (Kotlin usb-serial-for-android 3.12 via a Tauri mobile plugin, bytes bridged over JNI), TCP (std net), simulator (in-memory) | tauri-plugin-serialplugin 4.2 on both | The plugin is young (4 months). Our own Kotlin path is the proven pattern from the owner's earlier Android work. The trait lets us swap. | | D3 | **One worker thread per link** owns the transport; requests go through an mpsc queue with priorities (commands > alarms > polling); per-device backoff | async tasks | Matches "one master per bus" (R4). Blocking serial I/O stays off the tokio runtime. | | D4 | **Sample bus** = `tokio::sync::broadcast` of `Sample{device, tag, raw, value, unit, quality, age_ms, ts_source, ts_rx, seq, profile_version}` consumed by UI, historian, LAN, MQTT | each consumer polls | One source of truth; every consumer sees identical quality. | | D5 | **uPlot** for trends | ECharts, Chart.js | Small (~50 KB), fast for 100k+ points, supports null gaps natively. Final choice confirmed against research/02. | | D6 | **LAN server = axum** on the Tauri tokio runtime, bound to a chosen interface, self-signed cert per session (rcgen), token in URL/QR, only GET + WS routes | Tauri localhost plugin (no Android) | R22. There are no write routes at all, so nothing to misconfigure. | | D7 | **MQTT: plain JSON topics `buslink/{site}/{gw}/{device}/{tag}`** in the MVP; Sparkplug B later | Sparkplug B now | Sparkplug's protobuf/birth/death adds a lot for a phone gateway. Plain topics + seq + quality meet R23. Revisit after the MVP. | | D8 | **Command service** state machine: `Idle → Armed(timeout) → Previewed(frame) → Confirmed → Sent → ReadBack → Done/Failed`, single attempt, audit row per transition | direct writes | N1/R18. The only code path that may emit FC05/06/15/16 (enforced by a Kiro hook). | | D9 | **Historian**: SQLite WAL, batch inserts every 1 s, logging interval ≥ polling interval, min/max/avg rollups per minute for long trends | raw only | R20 and N3 (big ranges load quickly). | | D10 | **Android targetSdk 36**, minSdk 24, `connectedDevice` FGS started after USB permission | API 37 | Avoids the Android 17 local-network permission until it is handled (research/03). | | D11 | Windows packaging: NSIS with WebView2 bootstrapper + portable exe; Android arm64 APK (debug-signed for the hackathon) | MSI | NSIS works from our toolchain; MSI is not required. | ## Data model (historian) `sessions(id, started, app_version, platform)` · `devices(id, session, profile_id, profile_version, unit_id, link)` · `tags(id, device, key, unit)` · `samples(tag, ts_rx_ms, ts_src_ms, seq, raw BLOB, value REAL, quality INT, age_ms)` · `events(ts, kind, device, tag, severity, text)` · `commands(id, ts, device, fc, address, requested, encoded_hex, response_hex, readback, state, user_note)` · `outbox(seq, topic, payload, tries)` · rollups `samples_1m(tag, minute, n, min, max, sum)`. ## Security (N2) - **Threat surfaces:** the write path, LAN server, MQTT credentials, imported profiles/CSV, USB permission. - **Controls:** - A Kiro hook blocks write function codes outside `command/` and the simulator. - The LAN server has no write routes. - Profiles are data validated by JSON Schema (no expressions or scripts). - CSV export has a formula guard. - Secrets are kept in the OS keychain / Android Keystore. - **Default posture:** LAN and MQTT off until the user enables them. ## Test strategy - **Unit and property tests in `buslink-core`:** - CRC known vectors. - Encode→decode round trip for all FCs. - Decoder never panics on random bytes. - All word orders. - Quality transitions. - Command state machine. - Scheduler fairness with one dead device. - **Simulator integration tests:** multi-device poll, fault injection, gap rendering data. - **UI:** `tsc` + a headless Chrome check of the five acceptance journeys. - **Hardware:** an evidence matrix (Windows + CH343G + BGT-SMPS; Android A35 + OTG + BGT-SMPS).

TypeScript + uPlot] -- Tauri IPC --> Svc[App services] Svc --> Core[buslink-core
codec · scheduler · profiles · quality · command service] Core --> Tr{Transport trait} Tr --> SerW[Serial: Windows COM] Tr --> SerA[Serial: Android USB OTG] Tr --> TCP[Modbus TCP] Tr --> Sim[buslink-sim
in-process simulator] Core --> Hist[(SQLite historian)] Core --> Bus[Sample bus
broadcast channel] Bus --> UI Bus --> LAN[axum LAN server
read-only + WS] Bus --> MQ[MQTT publisher
outbox] end SerW & SerA --> RS485[USB-RS485 CH343G → RS485 bus → devices] TCP --> PLC[Modbus TCP devices] LAN --> Browser[LAN browser] MQ --> Broker[MQTT broker] ``` ## Repository layout ``` crates/buslink-core/ # protocol (RTU/TCP framing, CRC), codec, profile schema + validation, # scheduler (one queue per link), quality, alarms, command service, historian, export crates/buslink-sim/ # deterministic simulator: soil sensor, VFD, temperature controller, energy meter; fault injection src-tauri/ # Tauri shell: IPC commands, transports (Windows serial, Android USB), LAN server, MQTT src-tauri/gen/android/ # generated Android project + Kotlin USB permission / FGS src/ # web UI (TypeScript, Vite), shared by the desktop window, Android WebView and LAN browsers profiles/ # bundled device profiles (JSON) + schema video/ # Remotion demo video project docs/ # BMAD, design, verification, Kiro evidence ``` ## Key decisions | # | Decision | Alternatives | Why | |---|---|---|---| | D1 | **Own RTU/TCP framing in `buslink-core`**, reusing `rmodbus`-style pure codec ideas; no async transport crate in core | tokio-modbus | Core stays sync and testable with a fake transport (property tests on CRC/framing). Length-based RTU parsing (from FC and byte count) is robust against USB fragmentation on Android (research/03 risk table). | | D2 | **Transport trait** `open/configure/read(timeout)/write/flush/close` + detach event; implementations for Windows serial (`serialport`), Android USB (Kotlin usb-serial-for-android 3.12 via a Tauri mobile plugin, bytes bridged over JNI), TCP (std net), simulator (in-memory) | tauri-plugin-serialplugin 4.2 on both | The plugin is young (4 months). Our own Kotlin path is the proven pattern from the owner's earlier Android work. The trait lets us swap. | | D3 | **One worker thread per link** owns the transport; requests go through an mpsc queue with priorities (commands > alarms > polling); per-device backoff | async tasks | Matches "one master per bus" (R4). Blocking serial I/O stays off the tokio runtime. | | D4 | **Sample bus** = `tokio::sync::broadcast` of `Sample{device, tag, raw, value, unit, quality, age_ms, ts_source, ts_rx, seq, profile_version}` consumed by UI, historian, LAN, MQTT | each consumer polls | One source of truth; every consumer sees identical quality. | | D5 | **uPlot** for trends | ECharts, Chart.js | Small (~50 KB), fast for 100k+ points, supports null gaps natively. Final choice confirmed against research/02. | | D6 | **LAN server = axum** on the Tauri tokio runtime, bound to a chosen interface, self-signed cert per session (rcgen), token in URL/QR, only GET + WS routes | Tauri localhost plugin (no Android) | R22. There are no write routes at all, so nothing to misconfigure. | | D7 | **MQTT: plain JSON topics `buslink/{site}/{gw}/{device}/{tag}`** in the MVP; Sparkplug B later | Sparkplug B now | Sparkplug's protobuf/birth/death adds a lot for a phone gateway. Plain topics + seq + quality meet R23. Revisit after the MVP. | | D8 | **Command service** state machine: `Idle → Armed(timeout) → Previewed(frame) → Confirmed → Sent → ReadBack → Done/Failed`, single attempt, audit row per transition | direct writes | N1/R18. The only code path that may emit FC05/06/15/16 (enforced by a Kiro hook). | | D9 | **Historian**: SQLite WAL, batch inserts every 1 s, logging interval ≥ polling interval, min/max/avg rollups per minute for long trends | raw only | R20 and N3 (big ranges load quickly). | | D10 | **Android targetSdk 36**, minSdk 24, `connectedDevice` FGS started after USB permission | API 37 | Avoids the Android 17 local-network permission until it is handled (research/03). | | D11 | Windows packaging: NSIS with WebView2 bootstrapper + portable exe; Android arm64 APK (debug-signed for the hackathon) | MSI | NSIS works from our toolchain; MSI is not required. | ## Data model (historian) `sessions(id, started, app_version, platform)` · `devices(id, session, profile_id, profile_version, unit_id, link)` · `tags(id, device, key, unit)` · `samples(tag, ts_rx_ms, ts_src_ms, seq, raw BLOB, value REAL, quality INT, age_ms)` · `events(ts, kind, device, tag, severity, text)` · `commands(id, ts, device, fc, address, requested, encoded_hex, response_hex, readback, state, user_note)` · `outbox(seq, topic, payload, tries)` · rollups `samples_1m(tag, minute, n, min, max, sum)`. ## Security (N2) - **Threat surfaces:** the write path, LAN server, MQTT credentials, imported profiles/CSV, USB permission. - **Controls:** - A Kiro hook blocks write function codes outside `command/` and the simulator. - The LAN server has no write routes. - Profiles are data validated by JSON Schema (no expressions or scripts). - CSV export has a formula guard. - Secrets are kept in the OS keychain / Android Keystore. - **Default posture:** LAN and MQTT off until the user enables them. ## Test strategy - **Unit and property tests in `buslink-core`:** - CRC known vectors. - Encode→decode round trip for all FCs. - Decoder never panics on random bytes. - All word orders. - Quality transitions. - Command state machine. - Scheduler fairness with one dead device. - **Simulator integration tests:** multi-device poll, fault injection, gap rendering data. - **UI:** `tsc` + a headless Chrome check of the five acceptance journeys. - **Hardware:** an evidence matrix (Windows + CH343G + BGT-SMPS; Android A35 + OTG + BGT-SMPS).

# BusLink Studio: epics and sprint plan (BMAD phase 3–4)

Each epic becomes one Kiro feature spec in `.kiro/specs/<epic>/` and is executed by the `buslink-builder` agent. `ics-security-reviewer` reviews every epic commit, and the builder fixes its findings.

| # | Epic (Kiro spec) | PRD | Done when | Target (WIB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | `core-protocol`: RTU/TCP framing, CRC, codec, profile schema, quality model, scheduler, fake transport, property tests | R4–R9, R7 | `cargo test` green; PBT for CRC/framing/codec/order; dead-device fairness test | Nov 13 |
| E2 | `simulator`: in-process soil/VFD/temp/energy devices, fault injection, loopback RTU + TCP server | R10, R24 | Sim drives all E1 tests; VFD/temp state machines respond to writes | Nov 14 |
| E3 | `app-shell-desktop`: Tauri 2 app, Windows serial transport (VID:PID detect), sample bus, historian, CSV/XLSX/JSON export | R1, R3, R12, R20, R21 | Windows exe reads the simulator + the real BGT-SMPS on the CH343G; export opens in Excel | Nov 17 |
| E4 | `dashboard-ui`: connection center, ISA-101 live tiles, uPlot gap-aware trends, register inspector, alarms, i18n id/en, training mode | R12–R16, R24, N3, N4 | Headless Chrome journey 1 passes; WCAG checks; 360 px layout | Nov 21 |
| E5 | `commissioning-control`: command service state machine, ID/baud wizard, simulated VFD/temperature control panel, audit, reports | R17–R19, N1 | Journey 4 passes; the guard hook blocks writes outside `command/` | Nov 24 |
| E6 | `android-otg`: Kotlin USB plugin (usb-serial-for-android), permission, FGS, SAF export, APK | R2 | APK reads the real sensor on the A35 via OTG (journey 2) | Nov 26 |
| E7 | `lan-mqtt`: axum read-only LAN dashboard (token + TLS), MQTT 5 telemetry with outbox | R22, R23 | Journeys 3 and 5 pass | Nov 28 |
| E8 | `release`: NSIS + portable exe, APK, README/judge guide, evidence matrix, Remotion video, SolidCraft 3D, submission kit | N5, N6 | Release published; video < 3 min; Devpost submitted | Dec 2 |

**Readiness gate:** PASS.
- PRD, architecture and research are complete, and the hardware is available.
- **Risk to watch:** E6 (Android USB) is the largest unknown. Its spike task runs early, right after E1/E3, so it is never left to the last week.

</content>
</file>

<content>
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate BusLink Studio device profiles (schema v1), stdlib only.

Usage:
  python3 tools/hooks/check_profile.py profiles/soil/bgt-smps-8in1.json [more.json ...]
  echo '{"file_path": "profiles/x.json"}' | python3 tools/hooks/check_profile.py   # hook stdin form

The schema is described in docs/profiles/schema-v1.md. Keys are strict
(unknown keys are errors), so a profile cannot smuggle in scripts or
expressions: profiles are data, never code.

Exit codes: 0 = all valid (warnings allowed), 1 = at least one invalid file.
A path outside profiles/ or a non-.json file is skipped with exit 0.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
MAX_BYTES = 1_000_000

LEVELS = ("generic", "documented", "simulated", "hardware_verified")
CAP_LEVELS = LEVELS + ("unsupported",)
TABLES = ("coil", "discrete_input", "input_register", "holding_register")
TYPE_WIDTH = {"bool": 1, "u16": 1, "i16": 1, "bitfield": 1, "u32": 2, "i32": 2, "f32": 2,
              "u64": 4, "i64": 4, "f64": 4, "string": None}
WORD_ORDERS = ("ABCD", "CDAB", "BADC", "DCBA")
STD_BAUD = (300, 600, 1200, 2400, 4800, 9600, 14400, 19200, 38400, 57600, 115200, 230400, 460800, 921600)
ROLES = ("operator", "commissioner")
RISKS = ("low", "medium", "high")
COMMAND_KINDS = ("run", "stop", "setpoint", "reset_fault", "mode")
APPLY = ("immediate", "after_reboot", "unknown")
MAX_REGS_PER_READ = 125     # FC03/04 limit
MAX_BITS_PER_READ = 2000    # FC01/02 limit

ID_RX = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$")
PROFILE_ID_RX = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*$")
SEMVER_RX = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$")
DATE_RX = re.compile(r"^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$")
CONTROL_RX = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]")

TOP_KEYS = {"$schema", "$comment", "schema_version", "profile_id", "profile_version", "vendor", "model",
            "category", "firmware", "description", "support_level", "capabilities", "simulated_only",
            "source", "evidence", "transport", "registers", "commands", "comm_config", "notes"}
REQUIRED_TOP = ("schema_version", "profile_id", "profile_version", "vendor", "model", "support_level",
                "transport", "registers")
REG_KEYS = {"id", "name", "description", "table", "address", "doc_address", "type", "length", "word_order",
            "scale", "offset", "unit", "decimals", "valid_range", "invalid_sentinels", "bits", "access",
            "write", "poll", "source_page"}
WRITE_KEYS = {"min", "max", "step", "allowed_values", "risk", "role", "confirm", "readback"}
SOURCE_KEYS = {"document", "revision", "url", "pages", "retrieved", "publisher"}
HW_KEYS = {"date", "adapter", "platform", "firmware", "unit_id", "record", "result", "notes"}
RTU_KEYS = {"unit_id", "baud", "data_bits", "parity", "stop_bits", "response_timeout_ms", "inter_frame_ms"}
TCP_KEYS = {"unit_id", "port", "response_timeout_ms"}
CMD_KEYS = {"id", "kind", "label", "register", "value", "readback_register", "expected", "timeout_ms"}
CAP_KEYS = {"read", "write", "comm_config", "control"}


class Report:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.errors: list[str] = []
        self.warnings: list[str] = []

    def err(self, path: str, msg: str) -> None:
        self.errors.append(f"{path}: {msg}")

    def warn(self, path: str, msg: str) -> None:
        self.warnings.append(f"{path}: {msg}")


def _no_dupes(pairs):
    out = {}
    for k, v in pairs:
        if k in out:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate key '{k}'")
        out[k] = v
    return out


def is_int(v) -> bool:
    return isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool)


def is_num(v) -> bool:
    return (isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool)) and v == v and v not in (float("inf"), float("-inf"))


def keys(r: Report, path: str, obj: dict, allowed: set[str]) -> None:
    for k in obj:
        if k not in allowed:
            r.err(f"{path}.{k}", "unknown key (profiles are strict data; no scripts or expressions)")


def text(r: Report, path: str, v, *, max_len: int = 200, required: bool = True) -> None:
    if v is None:
        if required:
            r.err(path, "required")
        return
    if isinstance(v, dict):  # bilingual {"en": ..., "id": ...}
        keys(r, path, v, {"en", "id"})
        for lang in ("en", "id"):
            if lang not in v:
                r.err(f"{path}.{lang}", "required when the text is bilingual")
        for lang, s in v.items():
            text(r, f"{path}.{lang}", s, max_len=max_len)
        return
    if not isinstance(v, str) or not v.strip():
        r.err(path, "must be a non-empty string or {\"en\", \"id\"}")
        return
    if len(v) > max_len:
        r.err(path, f"longer than {max_len} characters")
    if CONTROL_RX.search(v):
        r.err(path, "contains control characters")
    if v[0] in "=+@\t\r":
        r.warn(path, "starts with a spreadsheet formula character; exports must escape it")


def enum(r: Report, path: str, v, allowed, required: bool = True) -> bool:
    if v is None:
        if required:
            r.err(path, f"required, one of {list(allowed)}")
        return False
    if v not in allowed:
        r.err(path, f"'{v}' is not one of {list(allowed)}")
        return False
    return True


def int_range(r: Report, path: str, v, lo: int, hi: int, required: bool = True) -> bool:
    if v is None:
        if required:
            r.err(path, "required")
        return False
    if not is_int(v) or not lo <= v <= hi:
        r.err(path, f"must be an integer {lo}..{hi}")
        return False
    return True


def check_source(r: Report, path: str, src) -> None:
    if not isinstance(src, dict):
        r.err(path, "must be an object")
        return
    keys(r, path, src, SOURCE_KEYS)
    text(r, f"{path}.document", src.get("document"))
    text(r, f"{path}.revision", src.get("revision"), max_len=80)
    url = src.get("url")
    if url is not None and (not isinstance(url, str) or not re.match(r"^https?://\S+$", url)):
        r.err(f"{path}.url", "must be an http(s) URL")
    if src.get("pages") is not None:
        text(r, f"{path}.pages", src.get("pages"), max_len=80)
    if src.get("retrieved") is not None and not (isinstance(src["retrieved"], str) and DATE_RX.match(src["retrieved"])):
        r.err(f"{path}.retrieved", "must be YYYY-MM-DD")


def check_transport(r: Report, path: str, t) -> None:
    if not isinstance(t, dict) or not t:
        r.err(path, "must be an object with 'rtu' and/or 'tcp'")
        return
    keys(r, path, t, {"rtu", "tcp", "simulator"})
    if not ({"rtu", "tcp", "simulator"} & set(t)):
        r.err(path, "needs at least one of rtu, tcp, simulator")
    rtu = t.get("rtu")
    if rtu is not None:
        p = f"{path}.rtu"
        if not isinstance(rtu, dict):
            r.err(p, "must be an object")
        else:
            keys(r, p, rtu, RTU_KEYS)
            int_range(r, f"{p}.unit_id", rtu.get("unit_id"), 1, 247)  # 0 is broadcast: never a device default
            baud = rtu.get("baud")
            if int_range(r, f"{p}.baud", baud, 300, 3_000_000) and baud not in STD_BAUD:
                r.warn(f"{p}.baud", f"{baud} is non-standard; Android CDC drivers may reject it")
            enum(r, f"{p}.data_bits", rtu.get("data_bits"), (7, 8))
            enum(r, f"{p}.parity", rtu.get("parity"), ("none", "even", "odd"))
            enum(r, f"{p}.stop_bits", rtu.get("stop_bits"), (1, 2))
            int_range(r, f"{p}.response_timeout_ms", rtu.get("response_timeout_ms"), 50, 10_000, required=False)
            int_range(r, f"{p}.inter_frame_ms", rtu.get("inter_frame_ms"), 0, 1_000, required=False)
    tcp = t.get("tcp")
    if tcp is not None:
        p = f"{path}.tcp"
        if not isinstance(tcp, dict):
            r.err(p, "must be an object")
        else:
            keys(r, p, tcp, TCP_KEYS)
            int_range(r, f"{p}.unit_id", tcp.get("unit_id"), 1, 255)
            int_range(r, f"{p}.port", tcp.get("port"), 1, 65535)
            int_range(r, f"{p}.response_timeout_ms", tcp.get("response_timeout_ms"), 50, 10_000, required=False)
    sim = t.get("simulator")
    if sim is not None and not (isinstance(sim, dict) and set(sim) <= {"model"} and isinstance(sim.get("model"), str)
                                and ID_RX.match(sim["model"])):
        r.err(f"{path}.simulator", "must be {\"model\": \"<simulator id>\"}")


def check_register(r: Report, path: str, reg, ids: set[str]) -> dict | None:
    if not isinstance(reg, dict):
        r.err(path, "must be an object")
        return None
    keys(r, path, reg, REG_KEYS)
    rid = reg.get("id")
    if not isinstance(rid, str) or not ID_RX.match(rid):
        r.err(f"{path}.id", "must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$")
    elif rid in ids:
        r.err(f"{path}.id", f"duplicate register id '{rid}'")
    else:
        ids.add(rid)
    text(r, f"{path}.name", reg.get("name"), max_len=80)
    if reg.get("description") is not None:
        text(r, f"{path}.description", reg.get("description"), max_len=500)
    table_ok = enum(r, f"{path}.table", reg.get("table"), TABLES)
    addr_ok = int_range(r, f"{path}.address", reg.get("address"), 0, 65535)
    da = reg.get("doc_address")
    if da is not None and not (is_int(da) or (isinstance(da, str) and 0 < len(da) <= 16)):
        r.err(f"{path}.doc_address", "must be the manual's label as a short string or integer")
    typ = reg.get("type")
    type_ok = enum(r, f"{path}.type", typ, tuple(TYPE_WIDTH))
    table = reg.get("table")
    width = None
    if type_ok:
        width = TYPE_WIDTH[typ]
        if typ == "string":
            if int_range(r, f"{path}.length", reg.get("length"), 1, MAX_REGS_PER_READ):
                width = reg["length"]
        elif reg.get("length") is not None:
            r.err(f"{path}.length", "only allowed for type 'string'")
        if table_ok:
            bit_table = table in ("coil", "discrete_input")
            if bit_table and typ != "bool":
                r.err(f"{path}.type", f"table '{table}' holds single bits; type must be 'bool'")
            if not bit_table and typ == "bool":
                r.err(f"{path}.type", "a register is 16 bits; use 'bitfield' with 'bits' for flags")
        wo = reg.get("word_order")
        if typ in ("u32", "i32", "f32", "u64", "i64", "f64"):
            enum(r, f"{path}.word_order", wo, WORD_ORDERS)
        elif typ == "string":
            if wo is not None:
                enum(r, f"{path}.word_order", wo, ("ABCD", "BADC"))
        elif wo is not None:
            r.err(f"{path}.word_order", f"not meaningful for single-register type '{typ}'")
        if typ != "bitfield" and reg.get("bits") is not None:
            r.err(f"{path}.bits", "only allowed for type 'bitfield'")
    bits = reg.get("bits")
    if bits is not None and isinstance(bits, dict):
        for b, label in bits.items():
            if not (isinstance(b, str) and b.isdigit() and 0 <= int(b) <= 15):
                r.err(f"{path}.bits.{b}", "bit index must be \"0\"..\"15\"")
            text(r, f"{path}.bits.{b}", label, max_len=80)
    elif bits is not None:
        r.err(f"{path}.bits", "must be an object of bit index -> label")
    if addr_ok and width is not None and reg["address"] + width - 1 > 65535:
        r.err(f"{path}.address", f"address {reg['address']} + {width} registers runs past 65535")

    scale = reg.get("scale", 1)
    if not is_num(scale) or scale == 0:
        r.err(f"{path}.scale", "must be a non-zero finite number")
    if reg.get("offset") is not None and not is_num(reg["offset"]):
        r.err(f"{path}.offset", "must be a finite number")
    if reg.get("unit") is not None and (not isinstance(reg["unit"], str) or len(reg["unit"]) > 16):
        r.err(f"{path}.unit", "must be a string of at most 16 characters ('' for dimensionless)")
    int_range(r, f"{path}.decimals", reg.get("decimals"), 0, 9, required=False)
    vr = reg.get("valid_range")
    if vr is not None and not (isinstance(vr, list) and len(vr) == 2 and all(is_num(x) for x in vr) and vr[0] < vr[1]):
        r.err(f"{path}.valid_range", "must be [min, max] with min < max (engineering units)")
    sen = reg.get("invalid_sentinels")
    if sen is not None and not (isinstance(sen, list) and all(is_int(x) for x in sen)):
        r.err(f"{path}.invalid_sentinels", "must be a list of raw integers")
    if reg.get("poll") is not None:
        enum(r, f"{path}.poll", reg.get("poll"), ("fast", "normal", "slow"))
    if reg.get("source_page") is not None:
        text(r, f"{path}.source_page", reg.get("source_page"), max_len=40)

    access = reg.get("access", "read")
    enum(r, f"{path}.access", access, ("read", "read_write"))
    w = reg.get("write")
    if access == "read_write":
        if table_ok and table not in ("coil", "holding_register"):
            r.err(f"{path}.access", f"table '{table}' is read-only in Modbus")
        if not isinstance(w, dict):
            r.err(f"{path}.write", "required for read_write registers (bounds, risk, role)")
        else:
            keys(r, f"{path}.write", w, WRITE_KEYS)
            enum(r, f"{path}.write.risk", w.get("risk"), RISKS)
            enum(r, f"{path}.write.role", w.get("role"), ROLES)
            if w.get("confirm", True) is not True:
                r.err(f"{path}.write.confirm", "explicit confirmation cannot be disabled")
            if w.get("readback", True) is not True:
                r.err(f"{path}.write.readback", "read-back verification cannot be disabled")
            av = w.get("allowed_values")
            has_bounds = "min" in w or "max" in w
            if av is not None:
                if not (isinstance(av, list) and av and all(is_num(x) for x in av)):
                    r.err(f"{path}.write.allowed_values", "must be a non-empty list of numbers")
            elif typ == "bool":
                pass
            elif not has_bounds:
                r.err(f"{path}.write", "numeric writes need min and max, or allowed_values")
            if has_bounds:
                lo, hi = w.get("min"), w.get("max")
                if not (is_num(lo) and is_num(hi) and lo <= hi):
                    r.err(f"{path}.write", "min and max must both be numbers with min <= max")
                elif vr is not None and isinstance(vr, list) and len(vr) == 2 and all(is_num(x) for x in vr):
                    if lo < vr[0] or hi > vr[1]:
                        r.err(f"{path}.write", "write bounds must lie inside valid_range")
            if w.get("step") is not None and not (is_num(w["step"]) and w["step"] > 0):
                r.err(f"{path}.write.step", "must be a positive number")
    elif w is not None:
        r.err(f"{path}.write", "only allowed when access is 'read_write'")
    if width is None or not table_ok or not addr_ok:
        return None
    return {"id": rid, "table": table, "start": reg["address"], "end": reg["address"] + width - 1,
            "writable": access == "read_write"}


def check_capabilities(r: Report, caps) -> dict:
    if caps is None:
        return {}
    if not isinstance(caps, dict):
        r.err("capabilities", "must be an object")
        return {}
    keys(r, "capabilities", caps, CAP_KEYS)
    for k, v in caps.items():
        if k in CAP_KEYS:
            enum(r, f"capabilities.{k}", v, CAP_LEVELS)
    return caps


def check_hardware_evidence(r: Report, ev) -> int:
    """Return the number of passing hardware test records."""
    if ev is None:
        return 0
    if not isinstance(ev, dict):
        r.err("evidence", "must be an object")
        return 0
    keys(r, "evidence", ev, {"hardware"})
    hw = ev.get("hardware", [])
    if not isinstance(hw, list):
        r.err("evidence.hardware", "must be a list")
        return 0
    passing = 0
    for i, e in enumerate(hw):
        p = f"evidence.hardware[{i}]"
        if not isinstance(e, dict):
            r.err(p, "must be an object")
            continue
        keys(r, p, e, HW_KEYS)
        if not (isinstance(e.get("date"), str) and DATE_RX.match(e["date"])):
            r.err(f"{p}.date", "required, YYYY-MM-DD")
        for k in ("adapter", "platform", "record"):
            text(r, f"{p}.{k}", e.get(k), max_len=200)
        if e.get("unit_id") is not None:
            int_range(r, f"{p}.unit_id", e.get("unit_id"), 1, 255)
        if enum(r, f"{p}.result", e.get("result"), ("pass", "fail", "partial")) and e["result"] == "pass":
            passing += 1
    return passing


def validate(doc) -> Report:
    r = Report()
    if not isinstance(doc, dict):
        r.err("$", "profile must be a JSON object")
        return r
    keys(r, "$", doc, TOP_KEYS)
    for k in REQUIRED_TOP:
        if k not in doc:
            r.err(k, "required")
    if "schema_version" in doc and doc["schema_version"] != 1:
        r.err("schema_version", "this validator understands schema_version 1 only")
    pid = doc.get("profile_id")
    if pid is not None and not (isinstance(pid, str) and 3 <= len(pid) <= 64 and PROFILE_ID_RX.match(pid)):
        r.err("profile_id", "must be 3-64 chars of a-z, 0-9 separated by . _ -")
    pv = doc.get("profile_version")
    if pv is not None and not (isinstance(pv, str) and SEMVER_RX.match(pv)):
        r.err("profile_version", "must be MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH")
    for k in ("vendor", "model"):
        if k in doc:
            text(r, k, doc[k], max_len=80)
    for k, n in (("category", 40), ("firmware", 80)):
        if doc.get(k) is not None:
            text(r, k, doc[k], max_len=n)
    if doc.get("description") is not None:
        text(r, "description", doc["description"], max_len=1000)
    if doc.get("notes") is not None:
        notes = doc["notes"]
        items = notes if isinstance(notes, list) else [notes]
        for i, n in enumerate(items):
            text(r, f"notes[{i}]", n, max_len=2000)

    level = doc.get("support_level")
    enum(r, "support_level", level, LEVELS, required=False)
    caps = check_capabilities(r, doc.get("capabilities"))
    sim_only = doc.get("simulated_only", False)
    if not isinstance(sim_only, bool):
        r.err("simulated_only", "must be true or false")
        sim_only = False
    if doc.get("source") is not None:
        check_source(r, "source", doc["source"])
    passing = check_hardware_evidence(r, doc.get("evidence"))

    claimed = [level] + list(caps.values())
    if "documented" in claimed or "hardware_verified" in claimed:
        if doc.get("source") is None:
            r.err("source", "documented / hardware_verified profiles must cite the manual (document, revision, pages)")
    if "hardware_verified" in claimed:
        if sim_only:
            r.err("support_level", "a simulated_only profile can never be hardware_verified")
        elif passing == 0:
            r.err("evidence.hardware", "hardware_verified needs at least one passing hardware test record "
                                       "(date, adapter, platform, record, result: pass)")
    if sim_only and level not in (None, "simulated", "generic"):
        r.err("support_level", "simulated_only profiles must be 'simulated' (or 'generic')")
    if level == "generic" and doc.get("source") is None:
        r.warn("source", "generic profile without a source; label it clearly in the UI")

    transport = doc.get("transport")
    if transport is not None:
        check_transport(r, "transport", transport)
        if isinstance(transport, dict) and "simulator" in transport and not sim_only and level == "simulated" \
                and not ({"rtu", "tcp"} & set(transport)):
            r.warn("simulated_only", "simulator-only transport; set simulated_only: true")

    regs = doc.get("registers")
    spans: list[dict] = []
    ids: set[str] = set()
    if regs is not None:
        if not isinstance(regs, list) or not regs:
            r.err("registers", "must be a non-empty list")
        elif len(regs) > 2000:
            r.err("registers", "more than 2000 registers")
        else:
            for i, reg in enumerate(regs):
                span = check_register(r, f"registers[{i}]", reg, ids)
                if span:
                    spans.append(span)
    by_id = {s["id"]: s for s in spans}
    spans.sort(key=lambda s: (s["table"], s["start"]))
    for a, b in zip(spans, spans[1:]):
        if a["table"] == b["table"] and b["start"] <= a["end"]:
            r.warn(f"registers.{b['id']}", f"overlaps '{a['id']}' in {a['table']} (alias? make sure it is intended)")
    writable = [s for s in spans if s["writable"]]
    if writable and caps.get("write") in (None, "unsupported"):
        r.err("capabilities.write", "profile has writable registers; declare the write support level")

    cmds = doc.get("commands")
    if cmds is not None:
        if not isinstance(cmds, list):
            r.err("commands", "must be a list")
        else:
            if not sim_only:
                r.err("commands", "control commands are only allowed on simulated_only profiles in schema v1 "
                                  "(no real VFD/heater control)")
            if caps.get("control") in (None, "unsupported"):
                r.err("capabilities.control", "profile has commands; declare the control support level")
            seen: set[str] = set()
            for i, c in enumerate(cmds):
                p = f"commands[{i}]"
                if not isinstance(c, dict):
                    r.err(p, "must be an object")
                    continue
                keys(r, p, c, CMD_KEYS)
                cid = c.get("id")
                if not isinstance(cid, str) or not ID_RX.match(cid) or cid in seen:
                    r.err(f"{p}.id", "must be a unique id matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$")
                else:
                    seen.add(cid)
                kind = c.get("kind")
                enum(r, f"{p}.kind", kind, COMMAND_KINDS)
                text(r, f"{p}.label", c.get("label"), max_len=80)
                reg = by_id.get(c.get("register"))
                if reg is None or not reg["writable"]:
                    r.err(f"{p}.register", "must name a read_write register of this profile")
                rb = c.get("readback_register")
                if rb not in by_id:
                    r.err(f"{p}.readback_register", "required; must name a register of this profile")
                if kind == "setpoint":
                    if c.get("value") is not None:
                        r.err(f"{p}.value", "setpoint values come from the operator, bounded by the register's write limits")
                elif kind in COMMAND_KINDS and not is_num(c.get("value")):
                    r.err(f"{p}.value", "fixed commands need a numeric value")
                int_range(r, f"{p}.timeout_ms", c.get("timeout_ms"), 100, 30_000, required=False)

    cc = doc.get("comm_config")
    if cc is not None:
        if not isinstance(cc, dict):
            r.err("comm_config", "must be an object")
        else:
            keys(r, "comm_config", cc, {"unit_id", "baud"})
            if caps.get("comm_config") in (None, "unsupported"):
                r.err("capabilities.comm_config", "profile has comm_config; declare its support level")
            for k, v in cc.items():
                p = f"comm_config.{k}"
                if not isinstance(v, dict):
                    r.err(p, "must be an object")
                    continue
                keys(r, p, v, {"register", "apply", "codes"})
                reg = by_id.get(v.get("register"))
                if reg is None or not reg["writable"]:
                    r.err(f"{p}.register", "must name a read_write register of this profile")
                enum(r, f"{p}.apply", v.get("apply"), APPLY)
                if k == "baud":
                    codes = v.get("codes")
                    if not (isinstance(codes, dict) and codes and all(
                            isinstance(code, str) and code.isdigit() and is_int(b) and 300 <= b <= 3_000_000
                            for code, b in codes.items())):
                        r.err(f"{p}.codes", "required: {\"<raw code>\": <baud>, ...}")
                elif v.get("codes") is not None:
                    r.err(f"{p}.codes", "only allowed for baud")
    return r


def load(path: pathlib.Path):
    data = path.read_bytes()
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        raise ValueError(f"file is larger than {MAX_BYTES} bytes")
    return json.loads(data.decode("utf-8"), object_pairs_hook=_no_dupes)


def path_from_stdin() -> str | None:
    if sys.stdin is None or sys.stdin.isatty():
        return None
    raw = sys.stdin.read()
    if not raw.strip():
        return None
    try:
        ev = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return None
    if not isinstance(ev, dict):
        return None
    for k in ("file_path", "filePath", "path", "file"):
        if isinstance(ev.get(k), str):
            return ev[k]
    ti = ev.get("tool_input")
    if isinstance(ti, dict):
        for k in ("path", "file_path"):
            if isinstance(ti.get(k), str):
                return ti[k]
    return None


def in_profiles(p: pathlib.Path) -> bool:
    try:
        rel = p.resolve().relative_to(ROOT)
    except ValueError:
        rel = p
    parts = pathlib.PurePath(rel).parts
    return p.suffix.lower() == ".json" and "profiles" in parts[:1]


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    any_path = "--any-path" in argv  # validate files outside profiles/ (self-tests, drafts)
    args = [a for a in argv if a and a != "--any-path" and "{{" not in a]  # unsubstituted {{filePath}} -> stdin
    if not args:
        p = path_from_stdin()
        if p is None:
            print("check_profile: no file given (pass a path or hook JSON on stdin)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 0
        args = [p]
    status = 0
    for a in args:
        p = pathlib.Path(a)
        if not p.is_absolute():
            p = (pathlib.Path.cwd() / p)
        if not any_path and not in_profiles(p):
            continue
        shown = a
        try:
            doc = load(p)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            continue  # deleted between save and hook run
        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
            print(f"INVALID {shown}: not valid JSON ({e})")
            status = 1
            continue
        rep = validate(doc)
        for w in rep.warnings:
            print(f"warning {shown}: {w}")
        if rep.errors:
            status = 1
            print(f"INVALID {shown}: {len(rep.errors)} error(s)")
            for e in rep.errors:
                print(f"  - {e}")
        else:
            n = len(doc.get("registers", []))
            print(f"OK {shown}: {n} registers, support_level={doc.get('support_level')}")
    if status:
        print("check_profile: profile schema v1 violations (see docs/profiles/schema-v1.md)", file=sys.stderr)
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

class Report:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.errors: list[str] = []
        self.warnings: list[str] = []

    def err(self, path: str, msg: str) -> None:
        self.errors.append(f"{path}: {msg}")

    def warn(self, path: str, msg: str) -> None:

def _no_dupes(pairs):
    out = {}
    for k, v in pairs:
        if k in out:
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate key '{k}'")
        out[k] = v

def is_int(v) -> bool:

def is_num(v) -> bool:

def keys(r: Report, path: str, obj: dict, allowed: set[str]) -> None:
    for k in obj:
        if k not in allowed:
            r.err(f"{path}.{k}", "unknown key (profiles are strict data; no scripts or expressions)")


def text(r: Report, path: str, v, *, max_len: int = 200, required: bool = True) -> None:
    if v is None:
        if required:
            r.err(path, "required")
        return
    if isinstance(v, dict):  # bilingual {"en": ..., "id": ...}
        keys(r, path, v, {"en", "id"})
        for lang in ("en", "id"):
            if lang not in v:
                r.err(f"{path}.{lang}", "required when the text is bilingual")
        for lang, s in v.items():

    if not isinstance(v, str) or not v.strip():
        r.err(path, "must be a non-empty string or {\"en\", \"id\"}")
        return
    if len(v) > max_len:

    if CONTROL_RX.search(v):

def enum(r: Report, path: str, v, allowed, required: bool = True) -> bool:
    if v is None:
        if required:
            r.err(path, f"required, one of {list(allowed)}")
        return False
    if v not in allowed:
        r.err(path, f"'{v}' is not one of {list(allowed)}")
        return False
    return True


def int_range(r: Report, path: str, v, lo: int, hi: int, required: bool = True) -> bool:
    if v is None:
        if required:
            r.err(path, "required")
        return False
    if not is_int(v) or not lo <= v <= hi:
        r.err(path, f"must be an integer {lo}..{hi}")

        r.err(path, "must be an object")
        return
    keys(r, path, src, SOURCE_KEYS)
    text(r, f"{path}.document", src.get("document"))
    text(r, f"{path}.revision", src.get("revision"), max_len=80)
    url = src.get("url")
    if url is not None and (not isinstance(url, str) or not re.match(r"^https?://\S+$", url)):

    if src.get("retrieved") is not None and not (isinstance(src["retrieved"], str) and DATE_RX.match(src["retrieved"])):

    rid = reg.get("id")
    if not isinstance(rid, str) or not ID_RX.match(rid):
        r.err(f"{path}.id", "must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$")
    elif rid in ids:
        r.err(f"{path}.id", f"duplicate register id '{rid}'")
    else:
        ids.add(rid)
    text(r, f"{path}.name", reg.get("name"), max_len=80)
    if reg.get("description") is not None:
        text(r, f"{path}.description", reg.get("description"), max_len=500)
    table_ok = enum(r, f"{path}.table", reg.get("table"), TABLES)
    addr_ok = int_range(r, f"{path}.address", reg.get("address"), 0, 65535)
    da = reg.get("doc_address")
    if da is not None and not (is_int(da) or (isinstance(da, str) and 0 < len(da) <= 16)):
        r.err(f"{path}.doc_address", "must be the manual's label as a short string or integer")
    typ = reg.get("type")
    type_ok = enum(r, f"{path}.type", typ, tuple(TYPE_WIDTH))
    table = reg.get("table")
    width = None
    if type_ok:
        width = TYPE_WIDTH[typ]
        if typ == "string":
            if int_range(r, f"{path}.length", reg.get("length"), 1, MAX_REGS_PER_READ):
                width = reg["length"]
        elif reg.get("length") is not None:
            r.err(f"{path}.length", "only allowed for type 'string'")
        if table_ok:
            bit_table = table in ("coil", "discrete_input")
            if bit_table and typ != "bool":
                r.err(f"{path}.type", f"table '{table}' holds single bits; type must be 'bool'")
            if not bit_table and typ == "bool":
                r.err(f"{path}.type", "a register is 16 bits; use 'bitfield' with 'bits' for flags")
        wo = reg.get("word_order")
        if typ in ("u32", "i32", "f32", "u64", "i64", "f64"):
            enum(r, f"{path}.word_order", wo, WORD_ORDERS)
        elif typ == "string":
            if wo is not None:
                enum(r, f"{path}.word_order", wo, ("ABCD", "BADC"))
        elif wo is not None:
            r.err(f"{path}.word_order", f"not meaningful for single-register type '{typ}'")
        if typ != "bitfield" and reg.get("bits") is not None:
            r.err(f"{path}.bits", "only allowed for type 'bitfield'")
    bits = reg.get("bits")
    if bits is not None and isinstance(bits, dict):
        for b, label in bits.items():
            if not (isinstance(b, str) and b.isdigit() and 0 <= int(b) <= 15):
                r.err(f"{path}.bits.{b}", "bit index must be \"0\"..\"15\"")
            text(r, f"{path}.bits.{b}", label, max_len=80)
    elif bits is not None:
        r.err(f"{path}.bits", "must be an object of bit index -> label")
    if addr_ok and width is not None and reg["address"] + width - 1 > 65535:
        r.err(f"{path}.address", f"address {reg['address']} + {width} registers runs past 65535")

    scale = reg.get("scale", 1)
    if not is_num(scale) or scale == 0:
        r.err(f"{path}.scale", "must be a non-zero finite number")
    if reg.get("offset") is not None and not is_num(reg["offset"]):
        r.err(f"{path}.offset", "must be a finite number")
    if reg.get("unit") is not None and (not isinstance(reg["unit"], str) or len(reg["unit"]) > 16):
        r.err(f"{path}.unit", "must be a string of at most 16 characters ('' for dimensionless)")
    int_range(r, f"{path}.decimals", reg.get("decimals"), 0, 9, required=False)
    vr = reg.get("valid_range")
    if vr is not None and not (isinstance(vr, list) and len(vr) == 2 and all(is_num(x) for x in vr) and vr[0] < vr[1]):
        r.err(f"{path}.valid_range", "must be [min, max] with min < max (engineering units)")
    sen = reg.get("invalid_sentinels")
    if sen is not None and not (isinstance(sen, list) and all(is_int(x) for x in sen)):
        r.err(f"{path}.invalid_sentinels", "must be a list of raw integers")
    if reg.get("poll") is not None:
        enum(r, f"{path}.poll", reg.get("poll"), ("fast", "normal", "slow"))
    if reg.get("source_page") is not None:
        text(r, f"{path}.source_page", reg.get("source_page"), max_len=40)

    access = reg.get("access", "read")
    enum(r, f"{path}.access", access, ("read", "read_write"))
    w = reg.get("write")
    if access == "read_write":
        if table_ok and table not in ("coil", "holding_register"):
            r.err(f"{path}.access", f"table '{table}' is read-only in Modbus")
        if not isinstance(w, dict):
            r.err(f"{path}.write", "required for read_write registers (bounds, risk, role)")
        else:
            keys(r, f"{path}.write", w, WRITE_KEYS)
            enum(r, f"{path}.write.risk", w.get("risk"), RISKS)
            enum(r, f"{path}.write.role", w.get("role"), ROLES)
            if w.get("confirm", True) is not True:
                r.err(f"{path}.write.confirm", "explicit confirmation cannot be disabled")
            if w.get("readback", True) is not True:
                r.err(f"{path}.write.readback", "read-back verification cannot be disabled")
            av = w.get("allowed_values")
            has_bounds = "min" in w or "max" in w
            if av is not None:
                if not (isinstance(av, list) and av and all(is_num(x) for x in av)):
                    r.err(f"{path}.write.allowed_values", "must be a non-empty list of numbers")
            elif typ == "bool":
                pass
            elif not has_bounds:
                r.err(f"{path}.write", "numeric writes need min and max, or allowed_values")
            if has_bounds:
                lo, hi = w.get("min"), w.get("max")
                if not (is_num(lo) and is_num(hi) and lo <= hi):
                    r.err(f"{path}.write", "min and max must both be numbers with min <= max")
                elif vr is not None and isinstance(vr, list) and len(vr) == 2 and all(is_num(x) for x in vr):
                    if lo < vr[0] or hi > vr[1]:
                        r.err(f"{path}.write", "write bounds must lie inside valid_range")
            if w.get("step") is not None and not (is_num(w["step"]) and w["step"] > 0):
                r.err(f"{path}.write.step", "must be a positive number")
    elif w is not None:
        r.err(f"{path}.write", "only allowed when access is 'read_write'")
    if width is None or not table_ok or not addr_ok:
        return None
    return {"id": rid, "table": table, "start": reg["address"], "end": reg["address"] + width - 1,
            "writable": access == "read_write"}


def check_capabilities(r: Report, caps) -> dict:
    if caps is None:
        return {}
    if not isinstance(caps, dict):
        r.err("capabilities", "must be an object")
        return {}
    keys(r, "capabilities", caps, CAP_KEYS)
    for k, v in caps.items():
        if k in CAP_KEYS:
            enum(r, f"capabilities.{k}", v, CAP_LEVELS)
    return caps


def check_hardware_evidence(r: Report, ev) -> int:
    """Return the number of passing hardware test records."""
    if ev is None:
        return 0
    if not isinstance(ev, dict):
        r.err("evidence", "must be an object")
        return 0
    keys(r, "evidence", ev, {"hardware"})
    hw = ev.get("hardware", [])
    if not isinstance(hw, list):
        r.err("evidence.hardware", "must be a list")
        return 0
    passing = 0
    for i, e in enumerate(hw):
        p = f"evidence.hardware[{i}]"
        if not isinstance(e, dict):
            r.err(p, "must be an object")
            continue
        keys(r, p, e, HW_KEYS)
        if not (isinstance(e.get("date"), str) and DATE_RX.match(e["date"])):
            r.err(f"{p}.date", "required, YYYY-MM-DD")
        for k in ("adapter", "platform", "record"):
            text(r, f"{p}.{k}", e.get(k), max_len=200)
        if e.get("unit_id") is not None:
            int_range(r, f"{p}.unit_id", e.get("unit_id"), 1, 255)
        if enum(r, f"{p}.result", e.get("result"), ("pass", "fail", "partial")) and e["result"] == "pass":
            passing += 1
    return passing


def validate(doc) -> Report:
    r = Report()
    if not isinstance(doc, dict):
        r.err("$", "profile must be a JSON object")
        return r
    keys(r, "$", doc, TOP_KEYS)
    for k in REQUIRED_TOP:
        if k not in doc:
            r.err(k, "required")
    if "schema_version" in doc and doc["schema_version"] != 1:
        r.err("schema_version", "this validator understands schema_version 1 only")
    pid = doc.get("profile_id")
    if pid is not None and not (isinstance(pid, str) and 3 <= len(pid) <= 64 and PROFILE_ID_RX.match(pid)):
        r.err("profile_id", "must be 3-64 chars of a-z, 0-9 separated by . _ -")
    pv = doc.get("profile_version")
    if pv is not None and not (isinstance(pv, str) and SEMVER_RX.match(pv)):
        r.err("profile_version", "must be MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH")
    for k in ("vendor", "model"):
        if k in doc:
            text(r, k, doc[k], max_len=80)
    for k, n in (("category", 40), ("firmware", 80)):
        if doc.get(k) is not None:
            text(r, k, doc[k], max_len=n)
    if doc.get("description") is not None:
        text(r, "description", doc["description"], max_len=1000)
    if doc.get("notes") is not None:
        notes = doc["notes"]
        items = notes if isinstance(notes, list) else [notes]
        for i, n in enumerate(items):
            text(r, f"notes[{i}]", n, max_len=2000)

    level = doc.get("support_level")
    enum(r, "support_level", level, LEVELS, required=False)
    caps = check_capabilities(r, doc.get("capabilities"))
    sim_only = doc.get("simulated_only", False)
    if not isinstance(sim_only, bool):
        r.err("simulated_only", "must be true or false")
        sim_only = False
    if doc.get("source") is not None:
        check_source(r, "source", doc["source"])
    passing = check_hardware_evidence(r, doc.get("evidence"))

    claimed = [level] + list(caps.values())
    if "documented" in claimed or "hardware_verified" in claimed:
        if doc.get("source") is None:
            r.err("source", "documented / hardware_verified profiles must cite the manual (document, revision, pages)")
    if "hardware_verified" in claimed:
        if sim_only:
            r.err("support_level", "a simulated_only profile can never be hardware_verified")
        elif passing == 0:
            r.err("evidence.hardware", "hardware_verified needs at least one passing hardware test record "
                                       "(date, adapter, platform, record, result: pass)")
    if sim_only and level not in (None, "simulated", "generic"):
        r.err("support_level", "simulated_only profiles must be 'simulated' (or 'generic')")
    if level == "generic" and doc.get("source") is None:
        r.warn("source", "generic profile without a source; label it clearly in the UI")

    transport = doc.get("transport")
    if transport is not None:
        check_transport(r, "transport", transport)
        if isinstance(transport, dict) and "simulator" in transport and not sim_only and level == "simulated" \
                and not ({"rtu", "tcp"} & set(transport)):
            r.warn("simulated_only", "simulator-only transport; set simulated_only: true")

    regs = doc.get("registers")
    spans: list[dict] = []
    ids: set[str] = set()
    if regs is not None:
        if not isinstance(regs, list) or not regs:
            r.err("registers", "must be a non-empty list")
        elif len(regs) > 2000:
            r.err("registers", "more than 2000 registers")
        else:
            for i, reg in enumerate(regs):
                span = check_register(r, f"registers[{i}]", reg, ids)
                if span:
                    spans.append(span)
    by_id = {s["id"]: s for s in spans}
    spans.sort(key=lambda s: (s["table"], s["start"]))
    for a, b in zip(spans, spans[1:]):
        if a["table"] == b["table"] and b["start"] <= a["end"]:
            r.warn(f"registers.{b['id']}", f"overlaps '{a['id']}' in {a['table']} (alias? make sure it is intended)")
    writable = [s for s in spans if s["writable"]]
    if writable and caps.get("write") in (None, "unsupported"):
        r.err("capabilities.write", "profile has writable registers; declare the write support level")

    cmds = doc.get("commands")
    if cmds is not None:
        if not isinstance(cmds, list):
            r.err("commands", "must be a list")
        else:
            if not sim_only:
                r.err("commands", "control commands are only allowed on simulated_only profiles in schema v1 "
                                  "(no real VFD/heater control)")
            if caps.get("control") in (None, "unsupported"):
                r.err("capabilities.control", "profile has commands; declare the control support level")
            seen: set[str] = set()
            for i, c in enumerate(cmds):
                p = f"commands[{i}]"
                if not isinstance(c, dict):
                    r.err(p, "must be an object")
                    continue
                keys(r, p, c, CMD_KEYS)
                cid = c.get("id")
                if not isinstance(cid, str) or not ID_RX.match(cid) or cid in seen:
                    r.err(f"{p}.id", "must be a unique id matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$")
                else:
                    seen.add(cid)
                kind = c.get("kind")
                enum(r, f"{p}.kind", kind, COMMAND_KINDS)
                text(r, f"{p}.label", c.get("label"), max_len=80)
                reg = by_id.get(c.get("register"))
                if reg is None or not reg["writable"]:
                    r.err(f"{p}.register", "must name a read_write register of this profile")
                rb = c.get("readback_register")
                if rb not in by_id:
                    r.err(f"{p}.readback_register", "required; must name a register of this profile")
                if kind == "setpoint":
                    if c.get("value") is not None:
                        r.err(f"{p}.value", "setpoint values come from the operator, bounded by the register's write limits")
                elif kind in COMMAND_KINDS and not is_num(c.get("value")):
                    r.err(f"{p}.value", "fixed commands need a numeric value")
                int_range(r, f"{p}.timeout_ms", c.get("timeout_ms"), 100, 30_000, required=False)

    cc = doc.get("comm_config")
    if cc is not None:
        if not isinstance(cc, dict):
            r.err("comm_config", "must be an object")
        else:
            keys(r, "comm_config", cc, {"unit_id", "baud"})
            if caps.get("comm_config") in (None, "unsupported"):
                r.err("capabilities.comm_config", "profile has comm_config; declare its support level")
            for k, v in cc.items():
                p = f"comm_config.{k}"
                if not isinstance(v, dict):
                    r.err(p, "must be an object")
                    continue
                keys(r, p, v, {"register", "apply", "codes"})
                reg = by_id.get(v.get("register"))
                if reg is None or not reg["writable"]:
                    r.err(f"{p}.register", "must name a read_write register of this profile")
                enum(r, f"{p}.apply", v.get("apply"), APPLY)
                if k == "baud":
                    codes = v.get("codes")
                    if not (isinstance(codes, dict) and codes and all(
                            isinstance(code, str) and code.isdigit() and is_int(b) and 300 <= b <= 3_000_000
                            for code, b in codes.items())):
                        r.err(f"{p}.codes", "required: {\"<raw code>\": <baud>, ...}")
                elif v.get("codes") is not None:
                    r.err(f"{p}.codes", "only allowed for baud")
    return r


def load(path: pathlib.Path):
    data = path.read_bytes()
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        raise ValueError(f"file is larger than {MAX_BYTES} bytes")
    return json.loads(data.decode("utf-8"), object_pairs_hook=_no_dupes)


def path_from_stdin() -> str | None:
    if sys.stdin is None or sys.stdin.isatty():
        return None
    raw = sys.stdin.read()
    if not raw.strip():
        return None
    try:
        ev = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return None
    if not isinstance(ev, dict):
        return None
    for k in ("file_path", "filePath", "path", "file"):
        if isinstance(ev.get(k), str):
            return ev[k]
    ti = ev.get("tool_input")
    if isinstance(ti, dict):
        for k in ("path", "file_path"):
            if isinstance(ti.get(k), str):
                return ti[k]
    return None


def in_profiles(p: pathlib.Path) -> bool:
    try:
        rel = p.resolve().relative_to(ROOT)
    except ValueError:
        rel = p
    parts = pathlib.PurePath(rel).parts
    return p.suffix.lower() == ".json" and "profiles" in parts[:1]


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    any_path = "--any-path" in argv  # validate files outside profiles/ (self-tests, drafts)
    args = [a for a in argv if a and a != "--any-path" and "{{" not in a]  # unsubstituted {{filePath}} -> stdin
    if not args:
        p = path_from_stdin()
        if p is None:
            print("check_profile: no file given (pass a path or hook JSON on stdin)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 0
        args = [p]
    status = 0
    for a in args:
        p = pathlib.Path(a)
        if not p.is_absolute():
            p = (pathlib.Path.cwd() / p)
        if not any_path and not in_profiles(p):
            continue
        shown = a
        try:
            doc = load(p)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            continue  # deleted between save and hook run
        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
            print(f"INVALID {shown}: not valid JSON ({e})")
            status = 1
            continue
        rep = validate(doc)
        for w in rep.warnings:
            print(f"warning {shown}: {w}")
        if rep.errors:
            status = 1
            print(f"INVALID {shown}: {len(rep.errors)} error(s)")
            for e in rep.errors:
                print(f"  - {e}")
        else:
            n = len(doc.get("registers", []))
            print(f"OK {shown}: {n} registers, support_level={doc.get('support_level')}")
    if status:
        print("check_profile: profile schema v1 violations (see docs/profiles/schema-v1.md)", file=sys.stderr)
    return status


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PreToolUse guard for BusLink Studio file writes (stdlib only).

Kiro pipes the hook event as JSON on stdin:
  {"hook_event_name": "PreToolUse", "cwd": "...", "tool_name": "fs_write",
   "tool_input": {"path": "...", "text": "..."}}

Only the lines a write would ADD are inspected. The guard blocks (exit 2,
reason on stderr) when an edit:
  1. adds Modbus write function codes (FC05/06/15/16, FC22/23) or write API
     names (write_single_register, ...) in source code outside
     crates/buslink-core/src/command/**, crates/buslink-sim/** and tests;
  2. adds a write addressed to the broadcast unit ID 0 (anywhere except tests);
  3. adds something that looks like a secret (API key, token, MQTT password,
     private key). Generic `password = "..."` assignments are allowed in
     example/sample files; high-confidence key formats are blocked everywhere.

Parse problems fail open: a warning on stderr and exit 1 (Kiro shows the
warning and the tool still runs). See .kiro/steering/safety.md.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(os.environ.get("BUSLINK_ROOT") or pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2])

WRITE_TOOLS = {"fs_write", "fs_append", "str_replace", "write", "fsWrite", "fsAppend", "strReplace", "create_file"}

CODE_EXT = {".rs", ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".kt", ".kts", ".java", ".html", ".vue", ".svelte"}

# Paths (relative, POSIX) where Modbus write code is allowed to live.
WRITE_CODE_ALLOWED = (
    re.compile(r"^crates/buslink-core/src/command/"),
    re.compile(r"^crates/buslink-sim/"),
)
TEST_PATH = re.compile(
    r"(^|/)tests?/"                       # crates/x/tests/..., src/test/...
    r"|(^|/)tests\.rs$"                   # src/foo/tests.rs
    r"|_tests?\.rs$"                      # codec_test.rs
    r"|\.(test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?$"      # ui.test.ts, x.spec.js
    r"|(^|/)src/(test|androidTest)/"      # Android unit/instrumented tests
)
# The hook scripts and their fixtures describe the patterns they detect.
SELF_PATH = re.compile(r"^tools/hooks/")

WRITE_NAME = re.compile(
    r"(?i)\b("
    r"masked?_?write_?registers?"
    r"|read_?write_?multiple_?registers"
    r"|write_?(single_?|multiple_?)?(holding_?)?(registers?|coils?)"
    r"|generate_set_(holdings?|coils?)\w*"          # rmodbus request builders
    r")\b"
)
