26-**Waktu perangkat / Device time** pada header menampilkan tanggal dan jam lokal berjalan setiap detik, bukan waktu sampel terakhir. Tabel Riwayat menampilkan waktu terima terbaru dahulu; **Lebih lama / Lebih baru / Terbaru** menavigasi halaman dalam filter aktif. Grafik dan ekspor tidak dibalik; sinkronisasi LAN tetap memakai kursor sumber yang sama.
27-
28:Jendela Windows menyesuaikan ukuran awal dengan work area monitor, DPI, taskbar dan bingkai, lalu tetap dapat ditarik pada sisi/sudut atau dimaksimalkan. Tampilan awal dibuat ringkas: buka disclosure **Pengaturan serial / Serial settings**, **Berbagi ke Android / Share with Android**, **Register mentah / Raw registers**, atau catatan satuan saat diperlukan. Konten yang diperluas tetap dapat di-scroll, bukan dipotong.
29-
30-
31-## Membaca pada Windows
32-
33-1. Pertahankan wiring yang sudah berhasil. Manual menyebut merah = power+, hitam = GND, kuning = A, hijau = B. **Jangan hubungkan 12 V ke konektor/data USB.** Wiring fisik belum diperiksa dalam pengembangan ini.
34-2. Disconnect **Modbus Poll** sebelum aplikasi ini mengambil COM yang sama. Jangan gunakan dua pembaca sekaligus.
35-3. **Sambung otomatis / Auto connect** aktif secara default. Aplikasi mengenali hanya USB **CH340 VID `1A86`, PID `7523`**: memilih satu kandidat unik, atau satu kandidat CH340 dengan serial number yang diingat. Lebih dari satu kandidat tanpa pembeda unik → pilih manual; tidak ada probe generik ke semua COM. COM4 hanyalah observasi mesin asal, bukan port yang dikunci aplikasi.
36-4. **Deteksi COM / Detect COM** memperbarui enumerasi dan memberi kesempatan percobaan otomatis baru. Profil adapter dicoba sekali per putaran percobaan; enumerasi berkala tidak mengulang open pada kandidat yang sama. **Putuskan** menjeda auto-connect selama run saat ini; untuk mengaktifkan lagi, nonaktifkan lalu aktifkan pilihan auto-connect atau mulai ulang aplikasi. Tidak ada reconnect rapat/scan slave atau baud.
37-5. Untuk manual, pilih COM dan buka **Pengaturan serial / Serial settings**: Slave Address, Baud Rate, Data Bit, Stop Bit, Parity dan interval. Default Slave 1, 9600 baud, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, parity None, interval 1 detik. Klik **Hubungkan**; profil serial baru diingat setelah sample fresh tervalidasi, bukan hanya berhasil membuka COM. **Putuskan** melepaskan port.
38-6. Lampu **hijau** dengan label terhubung hanya berarti sample tervalidasi masih fresh, bukan sekadar port terbuka. Lampu/label menghubungkan atau terputus, umur data dan error tetap perlu diperhatikan. Nilai lama setelah timeout **bukan pengukuran baru**. Label koneksi gateway Android terpisah dari lampu pembacaan.
39-7. Lampu **Modbus TX/RX** terpisah dari lampu koneksi. TX menghitung byte yang benar-benar ditulis, RX byte yang diterima termasuk frame invalid; bukan indikator byte USB HP. Lampu berkedip 180 ms ketika counter baru berumur ≤800 ms teramati. Poll UI dapat melewatkan kedip; counter tetap informatif. RX menyala tidak otomatis membuat data fresh.
40-
41-Baud dapat dipilih dari saran umum atau diisi 300–1000000, data bits 5–8, stop bits 1/2, parity None/Odd/Even. Pilihan harus sesuai sensor dan dapat ditolak driver adapter. **Ini pengaturan koneksi aplikasi, bukan perintah untuk mengubah konfigurasi sensor.** Disconnect dahulu untuk mengganti konfigurasi. Pada baud rendah, deadline dan jeda antar-frame memperhitungkan waktu transmisi; default tetap seperti sebelumnya.
42-
43-## Android USB langsung — tanpa PC
44-
45-1. Colok converter CH340 melalui adapter OTG/data pengguna ke HP; sensor tetap memakai PSU12V sendiri. Tidak memerlukan USB debugging, tethering, Wi-Fi, IP atau pairing.
46-2. Buka app; default **Pengaturan → Sumber pembacaan → USB langsung · BGT-SMPS**. Satu CH3401A86:7523 unik dihubungkan otomatis. Izinkan prompt USB Android; pilihan app default dapat mengurangi langkah berikut, bukan jaminan tanpa dialog setelah reboot/OEM tertentu.
47-3. Default **slave1 / 9600 / 8N1 / FC03 PDU0 count8 / interval1000ms**. Profil serial diingat setelah sample fresh. Adapter terdeteksi bukan berarti sensor sudah merespons; tunggu lampu fresh dan cek error. Beberapa adapter → pilih manual. Deteksi USB bukan scan baud/slave.
48-4. Driver `usb-serial-for-android3.11.0` MIT dibundel dalam APK; tidak perlu driver Windows/root di HP. IzinUSB tetap wajib. Jika USBHost tidak dilaporkan OS, gunakan modeLAN; app tidak memaksa OTG atau melewati keamanan.
49-5. Putuskan menjeda auto selama run; aktifkan kembali auto/restart untuk melanjutkan. Cabut-pasang memberi kesempatan baru bila tidak dijeda manual. Penolakan izin tidak membuat loop prompt.
50-6. Sejak 0.7.0, USB tetap terbuka saat app di latar atau layar mati: layanan foreground dengan notifikasi tetap dan wake lock parsial menjaga pembacaan dan perekaman. Izinkan notifikasi (Android 13+) dan setel baterai aplikasi ke **Tidak dibatasi / Unrestricted**; beberapa OEM tetap dapat menghentikan aplikasi bila tidak. Layanan berhenti saat Putuskan, USB dicabut, jadwal selesai atau galat. Belum diuji pada HP fisik dengan sensor.
51-7. Data valid dicatat native dengan sumber/sesiHP, berbeda dari mirrorPC. Riwayat lama tidak dihapus; grafik/tabel/XLSX/CSV/JSON memakai database lokal yang sama. Putuskan dahulu sebelum mengganti USB/LAN.
52-
53-## Android melalui PC/LAN
54-
55-1. PC dan HP harus saling dapat dijangkau pada LAN privat. SSID sama belum menjamin koneksi bila client isolation aktif.
56-2. Pada Windows, buka **Berbagi ke Android / Share with Android**, masukkan IPv4 privat **milik PC**, pilih port (awal 8443), lalu **Aktifkan berbagi LAN / Start LAN sharing**. Aplikasi tidak membuka firewall atau port forwarding. Bila diblokir, administrator perlu membuat rule terbatas aplikasi/port pada jaringan privat; jangan mematikan firewall.
57-3. Buka **Tampilkan kode pairing**. Seluruh JSON adalah **rahasia sesi**: pemegangnya dapat membaca snapshot dan riwayat yang dibagikan. Pindahkan melalui kanal tepercaya; jangan unggah ke chat publik atau log.
58-4. Pada Android pilih **Pengaturan → Sumber pembacaan → LAN dari Windows (opsional)** setelah USB diputuskan; tempel JSON lalu **Hubungkan**. Berhasil pairing membersihkan input dan kembali ke Pembacaan. Android17/API37+ meminta izin jaringan lokal; jika ditolak permanen, tinjau Settings aplikasi.
59-5. Saat terhubung dan aplikasi berada di foreground, Android mengambil snapshot serta halaman riwayat TLS **maksimal 500 baris per refresh**, melanjutkan cursor sumber yang disimpan secara transaksional. Catch-up mengambil data PC yang tertinggal tanpa bergantung pada snapshot yang kebetulan terlihat di UI dan tanpa menambah transaksi RS485. Ini bukan sinkronisasi background atau jaminan langsung lengkap; biarkan tetap terhubung sampai tertangkap. PC tidur/aplikasi tertutup/LAN terputus → tidak ada data baru; riwayat yang sudah dicerminkan tetap dapat diakses offline.
60-6. **Matikan berbagi** menutup listener dan koneksi gateway. Mengaktifkan ulang membuat sertifikat/token baru; pairing lama tidak berlaku. Pairing tidak disimpan permanen. Perubahan IP PC memerlukan pairing baru.
61-
62-Mode LAN tidak membaca USB HP dan tidak memerlukan driver USB HP. Client memercayai sertifikat sesi pairing dan memeriksa identitasIP; TLS tidak dinonaktifkan.
63-
64-Konfigurasi serial LAN dipilih pada Windows, pemilik adapter. Konfigurasi USBAndroid hanya berlaku bagi adapter yang dipasang pada HP; tidak mengubah setting PC atau menulis sensor.
65-
66-## Riwayat, grafik dan ekspor
67-
68-- Windows mencatat **setiap sample valid pada worker native**, bukan saat layar merender. Penyimpanan durable append-only: `app_data_dir/history-v1.sqlite3`, dengan WAL/transaksi dan identitas sumber/sesi. Error penyimpanan/sinkronisasi ditampilkan; lampu fresh bukan bukti baris berhasil tersimpan. Tidak ada tombol hapus/reset riwayat.
--
71:- **Ekspor / Export** ke XLSX, CSV, JSON atau **Ringkasan** memuat **seluruh baris lokal dalam filter**, tidak dibatasi grafik/halaman. Termasuk waktu UTC ISO 8601 dan epoch milidetik, satuan, konfigurasi serial, interval baca/simpan, label sesi, delapan raw register/nilai, sumber/sesi/sequence. XLSX menambah lembar Events dan Summary; JSON skema 2 menyertakan `events` dan `stats`; Ringkasan adalah CSV statistik + kejadian. Teks pengguna yang diawali `= + - @` diberi apostrof di CSV. Ambiguitas satuan NPK tetap berlaku.
72-- Rekaman penelitian, jadwal, penanda dan batas alarm: lihat manual bagian **Rekaman penelitian**.
73-- Windows memakai dialog simpan OS; Android memakai **Storage Access Framework `ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT`** untuk menyalin hasil dari cache aplikasi ke tujuan pilihan pengguna. Tidak memerlukan izin storage luas/root. Batal bukan berhasil menyimpan; file ekspor bukan pengganti cadangan database penuh.
74-- Untuk cadangan SQLite, tutup aplikasi secara normal sebelum menyalin database; jangan mengambil hanya file utama ketika WAL masih aktif. Lindungi ekspor/cadangan dari kehilangan atau pembagian yang tidak diinginkan. Hapus data aplikasi Android dapat menghapus mirror/cursor lokal.
75-
76-## Panduan offline dan driver
77-
78-Tombol **Bantuan / Help** pada header Windows atau tab **Pengaturan** Android, serta **F1**, membuka manual HTML offline Indonesia/English. **Daftar isi / Contents** menuju bagian manual; **Escape**, **Tutup / Close**, atau Back menutup dialog dan memulihkan fokus. **Simpan PDF / Save PDF** memakai dialog simpan platform yang sama. Panduan memuat operasi, wiring, troubleshooting, pencadangan dan pemeliharaan; tidak memerlukan CDN/internet.
79-
80-- Indonesia: [panduan sumber](docs/manual-user-id.md), [HTML offline](public/manual-id.html), [PDF](public/manual-id.pdf).
81-- English: [manual source](docs/manual-user-en.md), [offline HTML](public/manual-en.html), [PDF](public/manual-en.pdf).
82-
83-- Panduan visual ringkas 12 halaman per bahasa: [Indonesia HTML](public/manual-visual-id.html), [PDF Indonesia](public/manual-visual-id.pdf), [English HTML](public/manual-visual-en.html), [English PDF](public/manual-visual-en.pdf).
84-- [Indeks gambar PNG](public/manual-images/index.html): 12 gambar Indonesia dan 12 English, masing-masing 1400 × 1800 piksel. Manual lengkap HTML/PDF di atas juga memuat seluruh halaman bergambar, diikuti rujukan teknis lengkap.
85-- Gambar antarmuka berasal dari frontend 0.7.0 dengan fixture sintetis terisolasi di browser; bukan bukti pengukuran atau dialog izin OS. Nama port dan angka contoh bukan konfigurasi universal.
86-- Regenerasi dokumentasi dengan Node 22+ dan Chromium yang **sudah terpasang**: `node scripts/render-manuals.mjs`. Opsional `CHROME_BIN=/path/to/chromium`. Script menghasilkan HTML visual, indeks, 24 PNG dan empat PDF secara offline; tidak memasang dependency atau membangun Rust/APK. Teks visual diedit di `scripts/generate-manual-visuals.mjs`, gaya di `public/manual-visual.css`, rujukan lengkap di HTML/Markdown manual.
87-- EXE/APK rilis lama belum memuat revisi manual ini. PDF aplikasi disematkan saat kompilasi; gunakan berkas `public/` yang diperbarui ini langsung, atau sertakan saat build rilis berikutnya. Jangan mengganti paket rilis/hash hanya untuk pembaruan dokumentasi.
88-
89-Installer Windows dikonfigurasi **per-machine** dan meminta administrator/UAC. Selain WebView2 offline, Windows-only bundle berisi paket CH340 x64 yang diekspor dari Driver Store mesin asal: `wch.cn 3.9.2024.9`, katalog bertanda tangan Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher. Hook installer memanggil PnPUtil untuk menambahkan paket dan membiarkan Windows memilih driver yang cocok; tidak memaksa downgrade/rebind. Hasil perlu restart diberitahukan tanpa restart paksa; kegagalan dilaporkan, bukan disamarkan sebagai driver siap. **Hook pemasangan tidak dijalankan selama pengembangan ini.** Uninstall aplikasi tidak menghapus driver bersama.
90-
91-Lihat [provenance dan batas redistribusi Windows](docs/operations/windows-driver-provenance.md). Katalog signed bukan installer signed, dan hak redistribusi publik payload ekspor belum terverifikasi; batasi installer Windows pada deployment privat. Tidak ada driverCH340 Windows dalam APK. AndroidUSB memakai library nativeAndroidMIT yang dibundel; modeLAN hanya memakai jaringan. Node/Rust hanya toolbuild.
92-
93:## Peta register
94-
95:| Register PDU | Parameter | Interpretasi | Satuan |
96-|---|---|---|---|
97-| 0 | Suhu | signed int16 / 10 | °C |
98-| 1 | Kelembapan | word / 10 | % volumetrik |
99-| 2 | EC | word | µS/cm |
100-| 3 | Salinitas | word | µS/cm sesuai manual |
101-| 4 / 5 / 6 | N / P / K | word | mg/kg sesuai contoh |
102-| 7 | pH | word / 100 | pH |
103-
104:Request ID 1: `01 03 00 00 00 08 44 0C`. Hanya FC03, start 0, count 8. Register 8/9 pada screenshot tidak dipakai karena tidak terdokumentasi.
105-
106-**Batas metrologi:** manual lokal menulis akurasi pH ±1 dan resolusi 0,01; dua desimal bukan akurasi 0,01. Satuan NPK juga ditulis `mg/kg(mg/L)` tanpa konversi yang jelas. Salinitas tidak dikonversi menjadi ppm/ppt. Nol NPK tidak otomatis berarti tidak ada hara. Komunikasi berhasil bukan bukti kalibrasi atau dasar rekomendasi dosis pupuk.
107-
108-## Alternatif pembaca
109-
110-Screenshot pengguna adalah **Witte Modbus Poll**, berbeda dari dua CLI berikut. Contoh satu kali baca ini bersifat dokumenter dan **tidak dijalankan ke sensor oleh agen**:
111-
112-```powershell
113-# modbusdriver modpoll: parity -p
114-.\modpoll.exe -m rtu -a 1 -b 9600 -d 8 -s 1 -p none -t 4:hex -0 -r 0 -c 8 -1 COM4
115-# epsilonrt mbpoll: parity -P
116-.\mbpoll.exe -m rtu -a 1 -b 9600 -d 8 -s 1 -P none -t 4:hex -0 -r 0 -c 8 -1 COM4
117-```
118-
119:Jangan menambahkan write-values setelah COM4. `-t 4` berarti holding register/FC03, bukan FC04. Tanpa `-0`, alamat pertama memakai `-r 1`. Software khusus resmi BGT-SMPS belum ditemukan dalam cakupan publik yang diperiksa; bukan bukti bahwa software tersebut tidak tersedia.
120-
121-## Debugging HP melalui USB-C
122-
123-Developer mode dan USB debugging adalah pengaturan berbeda. Screenshot awal menunjukkan `Blocked by Auto Blocker`; setelah pemilik mengatur HP dan mengotorisasi laptop, ADB mendeteksi Samsung SM-A356E Android16/API36. Pemasangan/start serta Help/Back/tema/bahasa dan PDF/ekspor SAF berhasil diuji pada HP. Tidak ada perubahan keamanan/driver oleh agen.

content.text:
Output:
127:The local manual, page 3, specifies DC 5–24 V; the product page specifies 12–24 V. A 12 V supply falls within both ranges, but this does not establish that your supply or wiring has been inspected. Match the unit label and supplier documentation before applying power. The manual defines these wires:
136:Table source: local BGT-SMPS manual, page 3. Colour alone does not replace checking the actual unit/adapter labels. Do not swap A/B while powered or connect supply voltage to A/B. Protect connectors, power supply, USB adapter, and PC from water: the sensor body's IP68 claim does not cover the entire installation.
194:Source: local manual page 4 for serial/protocol defaults; application specification for intervals. Application addresses are limited to 1–247. Other suggested baud/data/parity choices do not establish that the sensor supports all of them. **Changing serial options configures the application/adapter connection, not the sensor's baud, address, or registers.** Match previously reconfigured units to their own records. The application offers no register writes, `0xFE` recovery address, or all-address search.
250:- **Labels:** Experiment name, Plot/sample ID and Operator take up to 120 characters each; Notes take up to 2000. Leading and trailing spaces are removed. Labels are locked when the session starts, stored with the session, and appear on every row, export and LAN sync. Leave them blank if not needed.
301:Ranges of up to 2000 rows are drawn point by point. Larger ranges are drawn from stored per-minute or per-hour summaries, as a mean line with a min–max band. Per-minute summaries are used when the data in the range spans at most 1500 minutes (25 hours); otherwise per-hour. The chart caption reads "mean per 1 minute" or "mean per 1 hour" with the row count. The table, statistics and exports still use the raw rows. The band shows the lowest and highest value of each minute or hour; the mean line alone does not show brief peaks.
316:**Raw and value columns.** `raw_0`–`raw_7` are the original Modbus registers (unsigned 16-bit integers) exactly as sent by the sensor and are always included in every export. The eight columns after them (`temperature_degC` … `ph`) are the converted values of the same registers: temperature = signed raw_0 ÷ 10 (65,501 → −3.5 °C), moisture = raw_1 ÷ 10, EC/salinity/N/P/K = raw as is, pH = raw_7 ÷ 100 (700 → 7.00). The XLSX Metadata sheet and JSON `units.conversions` list each column pair and its formula, so the raw data can be reprocessed in other tools.
354:Check sensor power and the known correct address, baud, data bits, parity, and stop bits. Check A/B only with power off and technical assistance if needed. Do not scan addresses, issue broadcast/recovery commands, or change sensor registers. Wiring/noise may need a technician; the application does not establish installation quality.
383:| 3 | Salinity | word | µS/cm per manual |
387:Table source: local manual page 4 response example, not a new sensor reading. R3 salinity and R7 pH follow the byte/value table; the manual's narrative ordering is inconsistent. Registers 8/9 are unused.
389:The manual, page 3, states **pH accuracy ±1 pH and resolution 0.01 pH**. Accuracy and resolution differ; two displayed decimals do not guarantee that accuracy. NPK is written as `mg/kg (mg/L)` without a conversion basis; displaying mg/kg follows the example and does not establish equivalence to mg/L. Salinity is written as µS/cm: the application neither converts it to ppm/ppt nor establishes that it duplicates EC. Vendor range/accuracy claims have not been validated by this project.
391:Open questions include physical-unit/PDF revision match, NPK and salinity meaning/basis, official calibration/storage procedures, driver redistribution licensing, final clean-PC installer behaviour, physical Windows 10 acceptance, broader phone/adapter compatibility, and physical-phone USB background/screen-off recording. The user's successful actual USB sensor readings do not resolve these separate questions. This guide supplies no crop recommendations, good/bad soil thresholds, or fertilizer doses. Agronomic decisions require separate metrological validation.
397:- Wiring, specifications, defaults, and register map: Beijing Guoxinhuayuan, `Manual for BGT-SMPS Soil Multi-Parameter Sensor (2026-04-27土壤八合一新款).pdf`, pages 3–4, local project copy. The filename does not verify firmware revision.

<content>
*Figure 12.* Check USB/COM ownership and permission, known serial settings, power, freshness, local storage and battery policy. Save the exact error and version. Do not delete history, disable protection or change sensor registers.

## Safety and preparation

**Never connect 12 V to a USB connector or USB data wiring.** The sensor uses a separate DC supply; a USB–RS485 adapter is not automatically a suitable sensor supply. Preserve the wiring that already works. Disconnect power before moving wires, and ask a technician to check polarity and terminals if uncertain. Do not work on exposed mains-powered supply parts.

The local manual, page 3, specifies DC 5–24 V; the product page specifies 12–24 V. A 12 V supply falls within both ranges, but this does not establish that your supply or wiring has been inspected. Match the unit label and supplier documentation before applying power. The manual defines these wires:

| Colour | Function |
|---|---|
| Red | Sensor DC power+ |
| Black | GND |
| Yellow | RS485_A |
| Green | RS485_B |

Table source: local BGT-SMPS manual, page 3. Colour alone does not replace checking the actual unit/adapter labels. Do not swap A/B while powered or connect supply voltage to A/B. Protect connectors, power supply, USB adapter, and PC from water: the sensor body's IP68 claim does not cover the entire installation.

The manual gives a working environment of 0–50 °C, distinct from its temperature measurement range of −30–70 °C. Its 3-second power-on stabilization and response below 1 second are vendor specifications, not guaranteed readiness for every installation. Do not force probes into stones or pull the sensor by its cable. These handling precautions are general recommendations, not a validated vendor installation or calibration procedure.

## Windows and Android installation

### Windows

1. Obtain the current release package from the trusted maintainer. Compare supplied hashes; do not mix executable, manual and installer versions.
2. The application targets Windows x64, Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11, and requires WebView2 Runtime. The application installer includes an offline WebView2 installer; the standalone executable needs an existing runtime and driver and does not run driver provisioning. Use the setup package for one-time driver provisioning. A clean-PC offline installation has not been demonstrated in device testing.
3. Close other readers using the COM port, including Modbus Poll. Run the installer and review its destination. An unsigned application installer may trigger SmartScreen; a signed driver does not sign the application installer. Do not disable Windows protection. Cancel and contact the maintainer if the package origin or identity is unexpected.
4. The installer is intended for per-machine installation and stages the signed CH340 driver package using PnPUtil. This requires administrator rights/UAC approval. Approve only the expected action/package. Driver integration is scoped to the identified CH340 USB VID `1A86`, PID `7523`, not FTDI, CP210x, or every serial device. Check the catalog/publisher identity; do not disable signature enforcement or force this driver onto another device. Staging a package does not prove every device successfully binds to it.
5. If CH340 already works, do not replace/rebind its driver merely to experiment. Check Device Manager for the device name, Hardware IDs, COM number, and warning-free status. COM numbers may change; COM4 is only the earlier observation. Cancelling UAC or a driver failure may leave the application installed without a usable COM port. Ask an administrator to resolve the correct package.

If setup reports a required restart (result `3010`), save your work and arrange a restart; the installer does not force one. Result `0` means PnPUtil succeeded, not that a sensor is attached or that the package displaced a higher-ranked driver. Other results fail setup with an actionable message; application files already copied can remain, so this is not a rollback or a complete installation. Keep the error details, ask an administrator to review the installer details and `%WINDIR%\inf\setupapi.dev.log`, and rerun setup after resolving the policy/package cause. Do not delete a working driver or force a rebind.

The observed driver signature is not automatic redistribution permission. The payload and installer are restricted to this user's private deployment; public redistribution permission for the exact exported package is unverified. Do not publish or pass the package to others until the maintainer has reviewed the rights. There is no claim that driver/installer deployment has been proven on all PCs. End users do not need the Rust/Node development toolchain. Provenance, hashes, and rights details: `docs/operations/windows-driver-provenance.md`; Microsoft PnPUtil reference: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devtest/pnputil-command-syntax

### Android

Use the matching APK. Android7/API24 is the minimum target, not proof for every phone. Debug/internal packages are not Play Store production releases. Follow prompts/organizational policy; trust only the intended source and do not broadly disable protection. Update the same package/signature without uninstalling to preserve local data; consult version records for tested devices.

**No root or separate CH340 driver installer is required on the phone.** The app bundles USB serial driver3.11.0 with its MIT license in Help. Android still controls USB permission. Only LAN mode requests local-network permission where required; direct USB does not need it.

### Direct USB without a PC

1. Keep the separate12V sensor PSU; the converter receives5V USB from the phone. Preserve your sensor–converter A+/B− wiring. Separate supplies do not prove galvanic isolation; do not tie grounds or change wiring without module specifications.
2. Connect CH340 through a **USB-A female → USB-C male OTG/data adapter** to a USB Host-capable phone. A photo or5Gbps/5A label does not prove compatibility with every phone. USB does not supply12V to the sensor.
3. Open the app. Default **Settings → Reading source → Direct USB · BGT-SMPS**. A unique CH3401A86:7523 connects automatically. Allow Android USB access and choose a default app if offered. Permission may be requested again after detach/reboot or on some OEM devices; the app does not bypass security.
4. Initial profile: slave1,9600,8N1,FC03 PDU registers0–7,1second interval. Allow power-on stabilization (manual3seconds). With multiple adapters, select one and **Connect**. **Detect USB** refreshes inventory; it does not scan baud rates or addresses.
5. Permission denial does not trigger a repeated automatic prompt. Select Connect to try again. **Disconnect** releases USB and pauses automatic connection for this run; re-enable Auto connect or restart the app to resume. Detach/reattach permits a new attempt unless manually paused.
6. Valid samples are stored locally independently of screen rendering. Since 0.7.0, while the USB port is open, a foreground service with an ongoing notification and a partial wake lock keep reading while the app is in the background, including a document picker, or the screen is off. The screen stays awake only while the app is visible and USB is open, without changing the system timeout. The USB connection must still be opened from the app while it is open. Notification permission and battery settings are described in [Research recording](#research-recording).
7. Disconnect before changing source or serial settings. USB preferences are separate from Windows and remembered after a fresh sample. LAN does not open USB; USB does not use pairing.

If no adapter appears, check host/data capability, connections, permission and competing USB reader apps. Use LAN if the OS does not report USB Host. Do not routinely enable debugging or disable Auto Blocker. The app cannot guarantee control of vendor OTG toggles. Physical OTG acceptance is still required on your actual combination.

## COM and serial settings

### Selecting and connecting

1. Open the Windows application and choose Indonesia or English. Theme System follows the OS; Dark and Light are alternatives. These preferences are local to each device and do not preserve pairing credentials.
2. Use **Detect COM** to refresh the port inventory. Detection does not scan sensor addresses/baud rates and does not prove a sensor response.
3. Check the adapter name and Hardware IDs. Automatic selection uses only the known CH340 profile. If there is more than one candidate, insufficient identity, or no match, identify and select the COM port manually. Do not select the lowest COM number or blindly try every port.
4. Set **Save data every** below Port before **Connect**; it is visible without opening **Research recording**. Open **Serial settings**, match the unit configuration, then choose **Connect**. **Auto connect** is enabled by default and only connects a unique, unambiguous CH340 `1A86:7523` candidate. Disable it if you want manual opening only. One detected CH340 does not prove the correct sensor is attached. If uncertain, disable auto connection before attaching the adapter and identify the device first. New settings are remembered as validated only after a fresh sample succeeds.
5. Wait for a valid frame and fresh-data status. **Disconnect** stops the reader, releases the port, and pauses automatic connection for the current application run. Disconnect before changing settings. If a port disappears or a fatal error occurs, investigate before connecting again; do not rely on unattended reopening.

This COM section applies to Windows. Only one reader owns an adapter; Android direct USB replaces the PC as owner, not a second reader on the same bus. LAN mode creates no second RS485 reader. Auto-connect is not a background service.

### Factory defaults, not sensor-write commands

| Setting | Manual/application default |
|---|---|
| Slave Address | 1 |
| Baud Rate | 9600 |
| Data Bits / Stop Bits / Parity | 8 / 1 / None (8-N-1) |
| Application interval | 1 second; 2 or 5 seconds available |
| Read operation | FC03, PDU offset 0, eight registers |

Source: local manual page 4 for serial/protocol defaults; application specification for intervals. Application addresses are limited to 1–247. Other suggested baud/data/parity choices do not establish that the sensor supports all of them. **Changing serial options configures the application/adapter connection, not the sensor's baud, address, or registers.** Match previously reconfigured units to their own records. The application offers no register writes, `0xFE` recovery address, or all-address search.

## Lamp, status, and readings

Read lamp/error text on Readings. Android sample age, last PC receive time and session counters are under **Settings → Communication details**; Windows keeps them in the readings panel. Do not judge a connection by colour alone.

**TX/RX show communication activity, not connection status.** Direct USB counters come from phone USB–RS485 I/O; LAN counters come from the PC reader through its gateway. RX includes bytes later rejected by CRC validation. Brief pulses mark newly observed traffic, not animation or proof of valid measurement. Reduced motion preserves counters without flashing.
</content>
</file>
Note: To continue, use offset 200.

### Empty history, storage error, or incomplete export

Check the date range/time zone, source device, local count, sync progress, free space, and history errors. Ensure export uses the intended range. Do not delete the database to suppress an error. Preserve files and ask the maintainer for help with corruption/permissions. Provide application/OS version, time and zone, exact error, serial settings, adapter identity, and an export safe to share. Never include pairing tokens.

## Measurement limits and open questions

| PDU register | Parameter | Application decoding | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Temperature | signed int16 / 10 | °C |
| 1 | Moisture | word / 10 | volumetric % |
| 2 | EC | word | µS/cm |
| 3 | Salinity | word | µS/cm per manual |
| 4, 5, 6 | N, P, K | word | mg/kg per example |
| 7 | pH | word / 100 | pH |

Table source: local manual page 4 response example, not a new sensor reading. R3 salinity and R7 pH follow the byte/value table; the manual's narrative ordering is inconsistent. Registers 8/9 are unused.

Salinity is written as µS/cm: the application neither converts it to ppm/ppt nor establishes that it duplicates EC. Vendor range/accuracy claims have not been validated by this project.

Open questions include physical-unit/PDF revision match, NPK and salinity meaning/basis, official calibration/storage procedures, driver redistribution licensing, final clean-PC installer behaviour, physical Windows 10 acceptance, broader phone/adapter compatibility, and physical-phone USB background/screen-off recording. # Research 03: Platform facts — Tauri 2, Android USB-OTG, CH343/CH340, Rust crates

Checked 2026-11-11. Every row cites the source that was opened. "Interpretation" means I drew the conclusion from the source but the source does not state it outright. **UNVERIFIED** means I could not confirm it from a primary source.

## Summary

- The Waveshare USB TO RS485 (B) uses a CH343G and an SP485EEN. Direction switching is automatic, and the board has TVS/ESD protection and a 120 Ω resistor. It is **not isolated**.
- The CH343 (1A86:55D3) enumerates as standard CDC-ACM. On Windows 10/11 it gets a COM port from the inbox driver without any install. On Android, usb-serial-for-android and the Tauri serial plugin both drive it with their generic CDC-ACM driver, not the CH34x driver.
- Tauri is at 2.12.3. `tauri-plugin-serialplugin` 4.2.1 covers desktop and Android USB serial with drivers written in Rust.
- `tokio-modbus` 0.17 can run RTU over any async byte stream, and `rmodbus` 0.13 is a transport-free frame codec. A from-scratch codec is not needed.
- On Android, three things need planning: the `connectedDevice` foreground-service rules, the `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK` permission that applies once the app targets API 37, and the fact that most phones cannot charge while in OTG host mode.

| LAN dashboard | axum + WebSocket spawned on the Tauri tokio runtime, read-only routes, bound to an explicit interface | Same frontend build served to browsers. On Android, keep targetSdk 36 until local-network permission handling exists |
| Storage | `rusqlite` with `bundled`, WAL | Same code on Windows and Android aarch64 |
| Export | `rust_xlsxwriter` + CSV | Pure Rust, no C dependencies |
| MQTT | `rumqttc` with a `TlsConfiguration::Rustls` config from `rustls-platform-verifier` (Android) or native roots (Windows) | Avoids shipping static roots |

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Waveshare (B) is non-isolated, so ground loops or surges on site can damage the phone or laptop | Hardware damage, noisy comms | Say this clearly in docs and demo. Wire the GND terminal. Recommend an isolated adapter (Waveshare RS485 (C)/(E), FT232RNL isolated) for field work. Lab demo is fine |
| 120 Ω termination may be fixed on the board (row 19, UNVERIFIED) | A mid-bus adapter adds an extra terminator; marginal signal on long buses | Inspect the board. If fixed, document "connect adapter at bus end only" |
| CH343 bound to the inbox CDC driver vs the VCP driver gives different COM names and features | Users confused about which driver they have | Detect by VID:PID 1A86:55D3, not by friendly name. Document that no driver install is needed on Win10/11. VCP is optional |
| `android-usb-serial` is 4 months old with few users | Unknown driver bugs on real phones | Test early on 2–3 phones with CH343 and CH340. Keep the usb-serial-for-android Kotlin fallback behind a trait so you can switch |
| Plugin APIs block | UI or tokio stalls | Run port I/O in `spawn_blocking` or a dedicated thread. Bridge to async channels for tokio-modbus |
| RTU frame boundaries over USB-serial (fragmented reads, Android scheduling jitter) | CRC errors, false timeouts | Parse by expected length from function code and byte count, not by 3.5-char silence alone. Use per-request timeout ≥200 ms. Use `setReadQueue`-style buffering. Prefer ≤115200 baud on Android |
| Android FGS misconfiguration (API 34+) | `SecurityException` crash when logging starts | Declare `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_CONNECTED_DEVICE`, type `connectedDevice`. Start the service only after USB permission is granted and while in foreground. Also declaring `CHANGE_NETWORK_STATE` covers the prerequisite in the no-USB (Modbus TCP only) case |
| Play Console FGS declaration | Review delay if publishing | Record the required demo video (in-app connect to the adapter). For the hackathon, sideload the APK and skip Play |

## 4. Contradictions

- **Baud range:** the CH343 datasheet says up to 6 Mbps. The Waveshare (B) board is rated to 3 Mbps; the SP485EEN is likely the limit, though that is my inference. The low end is listed as 50 bps on the wiki and 300 bps on the product page.
- **Isolation:** one reseller (Kamami) URL slug says "isolated". The manufacturer pages do not, and Waveshare sells isolated models as separate SKUs.
- **Portable exe guidance** comes from a 2021 Tauri v1-era issue comment. Tauri 2 docs don't cover a portable mode beyond `appDirectoriesOverride`.

## 5. Missing evidence

- Whether the Waveshare (B) 120 Ω resistor can be disconnected (jumper or switch): UNVERIFIED.
- The exact first usb-serial-for-android version that handled a real CH343: inferred as v3.5.0. No release note names the CH343.
- Whether rusqlite PR #1592 (x86_64 Android) is in 0.42.0: UNVERIFIED.
- Vention CDQ current rating and whether any Vention OTG adapter does PD pass-through with data on a specific test phone: needs a bench test.
- Whether `tauri-plugin-serialplugin`'s Android path holds up on long (multi-hour) RTU polling: no field reports found.
- I did not see the Waveshare wiki live (403). The archived copy is from 2025-11-20 and the product page copy from 2026-02-13.

## 6. Next steps

1. Bench test: Windows 11 inbox CDC + CH343, and Android phone + Vention CDQ + Waveshare (B) + one Modbus slave. Use `tauri-plugin-serialplugin` and log CRC and timeout rates at 9600, 19200 and 115200 baud.
2. Photograph the (B) board to settle the 120 Ω jumper question.
3. Spike a Tauri 2.12 Android build with rusqlite (aarch64), rumqttc + rustls-platform-verifier, and axum bound to 0.0.0.0, to confirm the toolchain before feature work.

| Storage | `rusqlite` with `bundled`, WAL | Same code on Windows and Android aarch64 |
| Export | `rust_xlsxwriter` + CSV | Pure Rust, no C dependencies |
| MQTT | `rumqttc` with a `TlsConfiguration::Rustls` config from `rustls-platform-verifier` (Android) or native roots (Windows) | Avoids shipping static roots |
| Android background | One `connectedDevice` FGS, started from user action after `UsbManager.requestPermission()` | Meets the FGS prerequisite and avoids dataSync's 6 h cap |

## 3. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Waveshare (B) is non-isolated, so ground loops or surges on site can damage the phone or laptop | Hardware damage, noisy comms | Say this clearly in docs and demo. Wire the GND terminal. Recommend an isolated adapter (Waveshare RS485 (C)/(E), FT232RNL isolated) for field work. Lab demo is fine |
| 120 Ω termination may be fixed on the board (row 19, UNVERIFIED) | A mid-bus adapter adds an extra terminator; marginal signal on long buses | Inspect the board. If fixed, document "connect adapter at bus end only" |
| CH343 bound to the inbox CDC driver vs the VCP driver gives different COM names and features | Users confused about which driver they have | Detect by VID:PID 1A86:55D3, not by friendly name. Document that no driver install is needed on Win10/11. VCP is optional |
| `android-usb-serial` is 4 months old with few users | Unknown driver bugs on real phones | Test early on 2–3 phones with CH343 and CH340. Keep the usb-serial-for-android Kotlin fallback behind a trait so you can switch |
| Plugin APIs block | UI or tokio stalls | Run port I/O in `spawn_blocking` or a dedicated thread. Bridge to async channels for tokio-modbus |
| RTU frame boundaries over USB-serial (fragmented reads, Android scheduling jitter) | CRC errors, false timeouts | Parse by expected length from function code and byte count, not by 3.5-char silence alone. Use per-request timeout ≥200 ms. Use `setReadQueue`-style buffering. Prefer ≤115200 baud on Android |
| Android FGS misconfiguration (API 34+) | `SecurityException` crash when logging starts | Declare `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_CONNECTED_DEVICE`, type `connectedDevice`. Start the service only after USB permission is granted and while in foreground. Also declaring `CHANGE_NETWORK_STATE` covers the prerequisite in the no-USB (Modbus TCP only) case |
| Play Console FGS declaration | Review delay if publishing | Record the required demo video (in-app connect to the adapter). For the hackathon, sideload the APK and skip Play |
| Android 17 local-network enforcement at targetSdk 37 | Modbus TCP and the LAN dashboard break silently (TCP timeouts) | Target API 36 (meets the current Play rule). Before moving to 37, add an `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK` runtime request with a rationale screen |
| Phone cannot charge during OTG (Vention CDQ has no PD port) | Long logging sessions drain the battery | Document the limit. Offer a PD pass-through adapter (e.g. Vention CCBHB) only as "may work, device-dependent". Use a low-power logging mode (screen off, FGS running). Show battery % in the UI |
| OTG bus power to adapter | Brown-outs, disconnects ("Queueing USB request failed") | The CH343 board draws little (200 mA fuse). Avoid unpowered hubs. Show a reconnect state in the UI |
| USB permission lost after reboot with device attached (Google Won't Fix) | Logger does not auto-resume | Add VID/PID rows in `0x` hex to `device_filter.xml` (CH343 55D3, CH340 7523, CH9102 55D4). Set `directBootAware`. Re-request permission on app start |
| MSI cannot be built on Linux CI | No MSI from a Linux runner | Build on a `windows-latest` GitHub runner, or ship NSIS only |
| WebView2 missing on some Win10 PCs; "single exe" is not official | App fails to start | Ship the NSIS installer with `embedBootstrapper` (or `offlineInstaller` for air-gapped plants). Offer a raw exe as "portable, needs WebView2" and set `appDirectoriesOverride` |
| Tauri 2.12 bumped Gradle/Kotlin/MSRV | Build breaks with older toolchains or plugins | Pin Rust ≥1.90 and Tauri 2.12.x. Re-run `tauri android init`. Make sure custom plugins use `consumer-rules.pro` |
| rusqlite bundled on x86_64 Android emulator may fail to link | Emulator builds break | Build aarch64 only (`--target aarch64`). Test on hardware, since the emulator has no USB anyway |
| TLS roots on Android for MQTT | TLS handshake fails against public brokers | Use `rustls-platform-verifier` with its Gradle snippet, or bundle `webpki-roots` as a fallback. Allow a user-supplied CA PEM for private brokers |
| MPL-2.0 file in the plugin dependency tree | License surprise in an OSS release | MPL is file-level and compatible with MIT/Apache apps. Note it in THIRD_PARTY notices |
| Read-only LAN dashboard exposed on plant networks | Data leak or unwanted access | Off by default, explicit bind address, optional token in URL, no write routes, LAN-only warning in the UI |

## 4. Contradictions

- **Baud range:** the CH343 datasheet says up to 6 Mbps. The Waveshare (B) board is rated to 3 Mbps; the SP485EEN is likely the limit, though that is my inference. The low end is listed as 50 bps on the wiki and 300 bps on the product page.
- **Isolation:** one reseller (Kamami) URL slug says "isolated". The manufacturer pages do not, and Waveshare sells isolated models as separate SKUs.
- **Portable exe guidance** comes from a 2021 Tauri v1-era issue comment. Tauri 2 docs don't cover a portable mode beyond `appDirectoriesOverride`.

## 5. Missing evidence

- Whether the Waveshare (B) 120 Ω resistor can be disconnected (jumper or switch): UNVERIFIED.
- The exact first usb-serial-for-android version that handled a real CH343: inferred as v3.5.0. No release note names the CH343.
- Whether rusqlite PR #1592 (x86_64 Android) is in 0.42.0: UNVERIFIED.
- Vention CDQ current rating and whether any Vention OTG adapter does PD pass-through with data on a specific test phone: needs a bench test.
- Whether `tauri-plugin-serialplugin`'s Android path holds up on long (multi-hour) RTU polling: no field reports found.
- I did not see the Waveshare wiki live (403). The archived copy is from 2025-11-20 and the product page copy from 2026-02-13.

## 6. Next steps

1. Bench test: Windows 11 inbox CDC + CH343, and Android phone + Vention CDQ + Waveshare (B) + one Modbus slave. Use `tauri-plugin-serialplugin` and log CRC and timeout rates at 9600, 19200 and 115200 baud.
2. Photograph the (B) board to settle the 120 Ω jumper question.
3. Spike a Tauri 2.12 Android build with rusqlite (aarch64), rumqttc + rustls-platform-verifier, and axum bound to 0.0.0.0, to confirm the toolchain before feature work.

| 55 | rumqttc | 0.25.1 (2025-11-21), Apache-2.0. Default feature `use-rustls`; optional `use-native-tls` and `websocket` | [crates.io API](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/rumqttc?include=default_version) | High |
| 56 | rumqttc TLS roots | `TlsConfiguration::Simple { ca, .. }` requires a PEM CA (otherwise `NoValidCertInChain`). `TlsConfiguration::Rustls(Arc<ClientConfig>)` accepts any rustls config | [tls.rs source](https://docs.rs/rumqttc/latest/src/rumqttc/tls.rs.html) | High |
| 57 | System roots on Android | `rustls-native-certs` does not support Android. Use `rustls-platform-verifier`, which needs a small Kotlin component wired into Gradle from its Maven repo, or bundle `webpki-roots`, which are static and need manual updates | [rustls-native-certs #3](https://github.com/rustls/rustls-native-certs/issues/3), [rustls-platform-verifier README](https://github.com/rustls/
| 58 | rusqlite | 0.42.0 (published 2026-11-11), MIT. The `bundled` feature compiles SQLite from source | [crates.io API](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/rusqlite?include=default_version) | High |
| 59 | rusqlite bundled on Android | aarch64 builds. `x86_64-linux-android` (emulator ABI) failed to link with soft-float symbols in open issue #1380 (2023), which has a workaround. A fix PR #1592 exists; **UNVERIFIED** whether it shipped in 0.42 | [rusqlite #1380](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite/issues/1380), [PR #1592](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite/pull/1592) | Medium |
| 60 | XLSX writer | `rust_xlsxwriter` 0.102.0 (2026-10-29), MIT OR Apache-2.0, MSRV 1.88. Pure Rust; the `constant_memory` feature handles large logs | [crates.io API](https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/rust_xlsxwriter?include=default_version) | High |

## 2. Recommended stack (derived from the table)

| Layer | Choice | Why |
|-------|--------|-----|
| Serial, desktop + Android | `tauri-plugin-serialplugin` 4.2.x (from the Rust side, via `serialplugin-core`) | One API on both targets. Handles CH343 (CDC) and CH340. Kotlin only does permission. Fallback: a custom Kotlin plugin over usb-serial-for-android 3.12.0 |
| Modbus | `rmodbus` for framing + own async transaction loop, or `tokio-modbus` RTU/TCP client | Both are permissive licenses. tokio-modbus accepts any async stream |
| LAN dashboard | axum + WebSocket spawned on the Tauri tokio runtime, read-only routes, bound to an explicit interface | Same frontend build served to browsers. On Android, keep targetSdk 36 until local-network permission handling exists |
| Storage | `rusqlite` with `bundled`, WAL | Same code on Windows and Android aarch64 |
| Export | `rust_xlsxwriter` + CSV | Pure Rust, no C dependencies |
| MQTT | `rumqttc` with a `TlsConfiguration::Rustls` config from `rustls-platform-verifier` (Android) or native roots (Windows) | Avoids shipping static roots |
| Android background | One `connectedDevice` FGS, started from user action after `UsbManager.requestPermission()` | Meets the FGS prerequisite and avoids dataSync's 6 h cap |

## 3. Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Waveshare (B) is non-isolated, so ground loops or surges on site can damage the phone or laptop | Hardware damage, noisy comms | Say this clearly in docs and demo. Wire the GND terminal. Recommend an isolated adapter (Waveshare RS485 (C)/(E), FT232RNL isolated) for field work. Lab demo is fine |
| 120 Ω termination may be fixed on the board (row 19, UNVERIFIED) | A mid-bus adapter adds an extra terminator; marginal signal on long buses | Inspect the board. If fixed, document "connect adapter at bus end only" |
| CH343 bound to the inbox CDC driver vs the VCP driver gives different COM names and features | Users confused about which driver they have | Detect by VID:PID 1A86:55D3, not by friendly name. Document that no driver install is needed on Win10/11. VCP is optional |
| `android-usb-serial` is 4 months old with few users | Unknown driver bugs on real phones | Test early on 2–3 phones with CH343 and CH340. Keep the usb-serial-for-android Kotlin fallback behind a trait so you can switch |
| Plugin APIs block | UI or tokio stalls | Run port I/O in `spawn_blocking` or a dedicated thread. Bridge to async channels for tokio-modbus |
| RTU frame boundaries over USB-serial (fragmented reads, Android scheduling jitter) | CRC errors, false timeouts | Parse by expected length from function code and byte count, not by 3.5-char silence alone. Use per-request timeout ≥200 ms. Use `setReadQueue`-style buffering. Prefer ≤115200 baud on Android |
| Android FGS misconfiguration (API 34+) | `SecurityException` crash when logging starts | Declare `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_CONNECTED_DEVICE`, type `connectedDevice`. Start the service only after USB permission is granted and while in foreground. Also declaring `CHANGE_NETWORK_STATE` covers the prerequisite in the no-USB (Modbus TCP only) case |
| Play Console FGS declaration | Review delay if publishing | Record the required demo video (in-app connect to the adapter). For the hackathon, sideload the APK and skip Play |
| Android 17 local-network enforcement at targetSdk 37 | Modbus TCP and the LAN dashboard break silently (TCP timeouts) | Target API 36 (meets the current Play rule). Before moving to 37, add an `ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK` runtime request with a rationale screen |
| Phone cannot charge during OTG (Vention CDQ has no PD port) | Long logging sessions drain the battery | Document the limit. Offer a PD pass-through adapter (e.g. Vention CCBHB) only as "may work, device-dependent". Use a low-power logging mode (screen off, FGS running). Show battery % in the UI |
| OTG bus power to adapter | Brown-outs, disconnects ("Queueing USB request failed") | The CH343 board draws little (200 mA fuse). Avoid unpowered hubs. Show a reconnect state in the UI |
| USB permission lost after reboot with device attached (Google Won't Fix) | Logger does not auto-resume | Add VID/PID rows in `0x` hex to `device_filter.xml` (CH343 55D3, CH340 7523, CH9102 55D4). Set `directBootAware`. Re-request permission on app start |
| MSI cannot be built on Linux CI | No MSI from a Linux runner | Build on a `windows-latest` GitHub runner, or ship NSIS only |
| WebView2 missing on some Win10 PCs; "single exe" is not official | App fails to start | Ship the NSIS installer with `embedBootstrapper` (or `offlineInstaller` for air-gapped plants). Offer a raw exe as "portable, needs WebView2" and set `appDirectoriesOverride` |
| Tauri 2.12 bumped Gradle/Kotlin/MSRV | Build breaks with older toolchains or plugins | Pin Rust ≥1.90 and Tauri 2.12.x. Re-run `tauri android init`. Make sure custom plugins use `consumer-rules.pro` |
| rusqlite bundled on x86_64 Android emulator may fail to link | Emulator builds break | Build aarch64 only (`--target aarch64`). Test on hardware, since the emulator has no USB anyway |
| TLS roots on Android for MQTT | TLS handshake fails against public brokers | Use `rustls-platform-verifier` with its Gradle snippet, or bundle `webpki-roots` as a fallback. Allow a user-supplied CA PEM for private brokers |
| MPL-2.0 file in the plugin dependency tree | License surprise in an OSS release | MPL is file-level and compatible with MIT/Apache apps. Note it in THIRD_PARTY notices |
| Read-only LAN dashboard exposed on plant networks | Data leak or unwanted access | Off by default, explicit bind address, optional token in URL, no write routes, LAN-only warning in the UI |

## 4. Contradictions

- **Baud range:** the CH343 datasheet says up to 6 Mbps. The Waveshare (B) board is rated to 3 Mbps; the SP485EEN is likely the limit, though that is my inference. The low end is listed as 50 bps on the wiki and 300 bps on the product page.
- **Isolation:** one reseller (Kamami) URL slug says "isolated". The manufacturer pages do not, and Waveshare sells isolated models as separate SKUs.
- **Portable exe guidance** comes from a 2021 Tauri v1-era issue comment. Tauri 2 docs don't cover a portable mode beyond `appDirectoriesOverride`.

## 5. Missing evidence

- Whether the Waveshare (B) 120 Ω resistor can be disconnected (jumper or switch): UNVERIFIED.
- The exact first usb-serial-for-android version that handled a real CH343: inferred as v3.5.0. No release note names the CH343.
- Whether rusqlite PR #1592 (x86_64 Android) is in 0.42.0: UNVERIFIED.
- Vention CDQ current rating and whether any Vention OTG adapter does PD pass-through with data on a specific test phone: needs a bench test.
- Whether `tauri-plugin-serialplugin`'s Android path holds up on long (multi-hour) RTU polling: no field reports found.
- I did not see the Waveshare wiki live (403). The archived copy is from 2025-11-20 and the product page copy from 2026-02-13.

## 6. Next steps

1. Bench test: Windows 11 inbox CDC + CH343, and Android phone + Vention CDQ + Waveshare (B) + one Modbus slave. Use `tauri-plugin-serialplugin` and log CRC and timeout rates at 9600, 19200 and 115200 baud.
2. Photograph the (B) board to settle the 120 Ω jumper question.
3. Spike a Tauri 2.12 Android build with rusqlite (aarch64), rumqttc + rustls-platform-verifier, and axum bound to 0.0.0.0, to confirm the toolchain before feature work.

    def test_word_order_required_for_32_bit(self):
        self.assertError(mutate(SENSOR, lambda d: d["registers"][2].pop("word_order")), "word_order")

    def test_bad_word_order(self):

    def test_word_order_on_16_bit(self):

    def test_bool_in_register_table(self):
        self.assertError(mutate(SENSOR, lambda d: d["registers"][0].update(type="bool")), "bitfield")

    def test_string_too_long_for_one_read(self):

    def test_write_on_input_register(self):

    def test_cli_valid_and_invalid(self):

            good.write_text(json.dumps(SENSOR), encoding="utf-8")
            bad = pathlib.Path(tmp, "bad.json")
            bad.write_text(json.dumps(mutate(SENSOR, lambda d: d.update(support_level="hardware_verified"))),
                           encoding="utf-8")

            self.assertIn("OK", p.stdout)
            p = self.run_cli("--any-path", str(bad))
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
            self.assertIn("INVALID", p.stdout)

    def test_duplicate_json_keys(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
            f = pathlib.Path(tmp, "dup.json")
            f.write_text('{"schema_version": 1, "schema_version": 2}', encoding="utf-8")
            p = self.run_cli("--any-path", str(f))
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
            self.assertIn("duplicate key", p.stdout)

    def test_outside_profiles_is_skipped(self):
        p = self.run_cli("package.json")
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout, "")

    def test_hook_stdin_and_unsubstituted_placeholder(self):
        p = self.run_cli("{{filePath}}", stdin=json.dumps({"file_path": "src/main.ts"}))
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0)

Epic E1 (`docs/bmad/epics-and-sprint.md`). Crate: `crates/buslink-core` (pure Rust, no Tauri dependency).
Covers PRD R3 (framing part), R4, R5, R6, R7, R8, R9, R20/R21 (core part), N1, N2 and architecture decisions D1, D2, D3, D4, D8, D9.
Rules that always apply: `.kiro/steering/safety.md`, `.kiro/steering/modbus.md`.

Acceptance criteria use EARS. "The core" means `buslink-core`.

## Requirement 1: RTU framing and CRC (R5, D1)

**User story:** As a commissioning technician, I want every RTU frame to be built and checked exactly as the Modbus serial line spec says, so that a reading is never taken from a corrupted frame.

1. THE core SHALL compute CRC-16/MODBUS (init `0xFFFF`, reflected polynomial `0xA001`, no final XOR) and transmit it low byte first.
2. THE core SHALL produce `0x4B37` for ASCII `123456789` and the frame `01 03 00 00 00 08 44 0C` for unit 1, FC03, address 0, quantity 8.
3. WHEN an RTU ADU is encoded with a PDU that is empty or longer than 253 bytes, THE core SHALL reject it with an error.
4. THE core SHALL derive character time, t1.5 and t3.5 from the actual serial settings (start + data + parity + stop bits) and SHALL use the fixed 750 µs / 1.75 ms values above 19 200 baud.

## Requirement 2: length-based RTU response reception (R5, D1, research/03 risk table)

**User story:** As a field user on Android OTG, I want responses that arrive in USB-sized fragments to be reassembled reliably, so that fragmentation never shows up as CRC errors or false timeouts.

1. WHEN response bytes arrive, THE core SHALL compute the expected length from the function code and byte count (FC01–04: `5 + byte_count`; exception: 5; fixed echo replies: `4 + data length`) and SHALL accumulate partial reads until that length or the deadline.
2. WHEN the deadline passes before the expected length is received, THE core SHALL report TIMEOUT.
3. WHEN a complete frame has a bad CRC, THE core SHALL report CRC_ERROR and SHALL NOT decode any value from it.
4. WHEN a complete frame has a valid CRC but a different unit ID, an unexpected function code, or a byte count that does not match the request, THE core SHALL report DECODE_ERROR.
5. BEFORE each RTU request, THE core SHALL discard stale input by reading until quiet (no hardware purge), and AFTER each exchange THE core SHALL keep at least the inter-frame gap (≥ t3.5, ≥ 5 ms floor, configurable floor for Android) before the next request.
6. WHEN arbitrary bytes are fed to the response framer or any decoder, THE core SHALL NOT panic.

## Requirement 3: exception responses (R7)

1. WHEN a response function code equals the request function code with bit 7 set, THE core SHALL report EXCEPTION with the exception code kept (01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 08, 0A, 0B and unknown codes).
2. THE core SHALL provide a name for every standard exception code so that the UI can show "EXCEPTION 02 illegal data address".

## Requirement 4: Modbus TCP MBAP (R3)

1. THE core SHALL encode the MBAP header (transaction ID, protocol ID 0, length = unit + PDU bytes, unit ID), big-endian.
2. WHEN an MBAP header has a protocol ID other than 0 or a length below 2 or above 254, THE core SHALL reject it as a framing error.
3. THE core SHALL frame TCP responses by the length field and SHALL handle partial and coalesced reads.
4. WHEN a TCP response carries a transaction ID other than the one outstanding, THE core SHALL discard it and keep waiting until the deadline.
5. WHEN the MBAP stream can no longer be framed, THE core SHALL report the link as lost instead of guessing a frame boundary.
6. THE core SHALL keep RTU-over-TCP as a separate framing kind (RTU frames with CRC over a stream), never confused with MBAP.

## Requirement 5: read PDUs and spec limits (R5, R8)

1. THE core SHALL encode and decode FC01, FC02, FC03 and FC04 requests and responses.
2. WHEN a read request has quantity 0, more than 2000 bits (FC01/02) or more than 125 registers (FC03/04), or `address + quantity > 65 536`, THE core SHALL reject it before anything is sent.
3. THE core SHALL address registers by `table + zero-based PDU offset` only; a manual label (`40001`) SHALL never be used as an address. The table SHALL be chosen by the function code.
4. Write PDUs (FC05/06/15/16) SHALL be encoded only inside `crates/buslink-core/src/command/` (safety rule 2).

## Requirement 6: data codec (R6)

1. THE core SHALL decode and encode `bool`, `u16`, `i16`, `bitfield`, `u32`, `i32`, `f32`, `u64`, `i64`, `f64` and `string` values from 16-bit big-endian registers.
2. THE core SHALL support the word orders ABCD, CDAB, BADC and DCBA for 32- and 64-bit types, applying word swap (register reversal) and byte swap (inside each register) as defined in `modbus.md`; strings SHALL support ABCD and BADC.
3. WHEN the number of registers does not match the type width, THE core SHALL return DECODE_ERROR instead of panicking.
4. THE core SHALL keep 64-bit integers exact (no conversion through `f64` for the raw value).

## Requirement 7: engineering values, range and sentinels (R6, R7)

1. THE core SHALL compute `engineering = raw × scale + offset` and SHALL support no other expression.
2. WHEN the raw value equals an `invalid_sentinels` entry, the result is not finite, or the engineering value is outside `valid_range`, THE core SHALL report DECODE_ERROR and keep the raw value.
3. WHEN an engineering value is converted back to raw for a command, THE core SHALL reject values that are not exactly representable in the register type (never round or clamp silently).

## Requirement 8: profile schema and validation (R9, N2)

1. THE core SHALL ship a JSON Schema (`profiles/schema/buslink-profile.schema.json`) for profile schema v1 and Rust types for every field.
2. WHEN a profile is loaded, THE core SHALL validate it with the same rules as `tools/hooks/check_profile.py`: strict keys, duplicate JSON keys rejected, support levels `generic | documented | simulated | hardware_verified`, `source` required for documented/hardware-verified, passing hardware evidence required for `hardware_verified`, unit ID 0 never a default, word order explicit for multi-register types, write bounds inside `valid_range`, commands only on `simulated_only` profiles.
3. THE Rust validator and the Python hook validator SHALL agree (same valid/invalid verdict and the same error paths) on every bundled profile and on a shared fixture set.
4. WHEN a profile file is larger than 1 MB, THE core SHALL reject it without parsing.
5. Profiles SHALL be data only: no scripts, no expressions beyond `raw × scale + offset`.

## Requirement 9: device instance versus profile (R9, R4)

1. THE core SHALL keep site settings (device ID, name, link, unit ID, poll interval, stale threshold, block-merging limits) in a device instance that references a profile by ID and version.
2. WHEN a device instance has unit ID 0, or a unit ID above 247 on an RTU link, THE core SHALL reject it.
3. WHEN a device instance references a profile with a different ID or version than the one supplied, THE core SHALL reject the pairing.

## Requirement 10: quality and age (R7)

1. Every sample SHALL carry one quality: GOOD, TIMEOUT, CRC_ERROR, EXCEPTION(code), STALE, DECODE_ERROR or DISCONNECTED, plus `age_ms`, a receive timestamp and an optional source timestamp.
2. WHEN a read fails, THE core SHALL keep the last good value with its original timestamp, and its age SHALL keep growing; the failed sample SHALL NOT carry a fresh timestamp for that value or a substitute zero.
3. WHEN a GOOD value is older than the stale threshold (default `max(3 × poll interval, 3 s)`) and no newer result exists, THE core SHALL emit STALE.
4. THE core SHALL map qualities to the OPC UA classes Good / Uncertain / Bad.

## Requirement 11: transports (R3, D2)

1. THE core SHALL define a `Transport` trait with write, read-with-timeout (a zero-byte timed read is a timeout, not end of stream), drain and close, and a disconnected error for detach.
2. THE core SHALL provide a scripted `FakeTransport` driven by a manual clock so protocol and scheduler tests are deterministic and do not sleep.
3. THE core SHALL provide a Modbus TCP client transport over `std::net`.
4. THE core SHALL refuse to open a second worker for a link key that is already owned (one master per bus).

## Requirement 12: one worker per link with a priority queue (R4, D3)

1. THE core SHALL run one worker per link that owns the transport; every read and write for that link SHALL go through its single queue.
2. THE worker SHALL serve commands before alarm reads and alarm reads before polling.
3. WHEN a command frame is executed, THE worker SHALL send it exactly once and SHALL NOT retry it, whatever the outcome.
4. WHEN the transport reports a lost link, THE worker SHALL mark every device on it DISCONNECTED, fail queued requests, and stop polling.

## Requirement 13: block merging (R5)

1. THE core SHALL merge registers of the same table into one read when they are contiguous (or within a configured maximum gap) and the block stays within 125 registers / 2000 bits, or a smaller device limit.
2. THE core SHALL never split one tag across two reads and SHALL never read an address that no tag covers unless the device's maximum gap explicitly allows it.

## Requirement 14: backoff and fairness (R4)

1. WHEN a device times out, THE core SHALL abort the rest of its cycle and back off exponentially (poll interval × 2ⁿ, capped, default cap 30 s); a successful cycle SHALL reset the backoff.
2. Reads MAY be retried a bounded number of times (default 1, only on timeout/CRC error, only when the device is not already in backoff). Writes are never retried.
3. WHILE one or more devices on a link are dead, every healthy device SHALL still be polled within `poll interval + Σ(other devices' blocks × (retries + 1) × timeout)`.
4. THE core SHALL count requests, GOOD results, timeouts, CRC errors, exceptions, decode errors, the last error and the achieved cycle time per device.

## Requirement 15: sample bus (D4)

1. THE core SHALL publish every sample on one broadcast bus so that UI, historian, LAN view and MQTT see identical values and qualities.
2. WHEN a subscriber lags behind, THE bus SHALL report the number of lost samples to that subscriber instead of dropping them silently.

## Requirement 16: command service (N1, R18, D8)

1. THE command service SHALL be the only code that builds FC05/06/15/16 PDUs.
2. THE command service SHALL follow `Idle → Armed → Previewed → Confirmed → Sent → ReadBack → Done | Failed`, with a single attempt per confirmation.
3. WHEN an operator arms a device, THE arming SHALL expire after 60 s idle (configurable) and SHALL be dropped on disconnect, reconnect, profile change or app background.
4. WHEN a command is previewed, THE service SHALL check, in order, arming, role, writability, bounds (`min`/`max`/`step`/`allowed_values`, reject never clamp), unit ID ≠ 0, and SHALL return a preview with device, unit ID, register doc address and PDU offset, old value, new value in engineering units, raw value and the encoded frame.
5. THE service SHALL send only after `confirm` with the ID of the current preview, and SHALL send at most once per confirmation.
6. AFTER sending, THE service SHALL read back and report verified, mismatch or unknown; a timed-out write SHALL be reported as effect unknown (read back, never retried).
7. Every transition SHALL append an audit record (time UTC, session, user, role, device, profile ID + version, function, address, old value, requested value, raw request, raw response or exception, read-back result); WHEN the audit record cannot be stored before sending, THE service SHALL NOT send.
8. Named profile commands SHALL only run on `simulated_only` profiles connected to a simulator link.
9. Acknowledgement and read-back SHALL be reported as separate fields (write acknowledged ≠ process reached target).

## Requirement 17: historian (R20, D9)

1. THE core SHALL store sessions, devices, tags, samples, events, command audit and outbox tables in SQLite (bundled) in WAL mode.
2. Non-GOOD samples SHALL be stored with their quality and a NULL value so that trends break at gaps.
3. THE command audit table SHALL be append-only (updates and deletes rejected by the database).
4. THE core SHALL insert samples in batches, apply a logging interval separate from the poll interval (quality changes always stored), and compute per-minute min/max/sum/count rollups from GOOD samples only.
5. Raw values SHALL be stored losslessly (registers as bytes, 64-bit integers exact).

## Requirement 18: export (R21, N2)

1. THE core SHALL export CSV (UTF-8, ISO-8601 UTC, quality, exception code and age columns), XLSX (sheets Measurements, Devices, Configuration, Events, Commands; numbers as numbers) and JSON (64-bit integers as strings).
2. WHEN a text cell starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or carriage return, THE export SHALL prefix it with `'` in CSV and XLSX.
3. Every exported measurement SHALL include the profile ID and version.
4. Exports SHALL never contain secrets.

1. THE core SHALL decode and encode `bool`, `u16`, `i16`, `bitfield`, `u32`, `i32`, `f32`, `u64`, `i64`, `f64` and `string` values from 16-bit big-endian registers.
2. THE core SHALL support the word orders ABCD, CDAB, BADC and DCBA for 32- and 64-bit types, applying word swap (register reversal) and byte swap (inside each register) as defined in `modbus.md`; strings SHALL support ABCD and BADC.
3. WHEN the number of registers does not match the type width, THE core SHALL return DECODE_ERROR instead of panicking.
4. THE core SHALL keep 64-bit integers exact (no conversion through `f64` for the raw value).

## Requirement 7: engineering values, range and sentinels (R6, R7)

1. THE core SHALL compute `engineering = raw × scale + offset` and SHALL support no other expression.
2. WHEN the raw value equals an `invalid_sentinels` entry, the result is not finite, or the engineering value is outside `valid_range`, THE core SHALL report DECODE_ERROR and keep the raw value.
3. WHEN an engineering value is converted back to raw for a command, THE core SHALL reject values that are not exactly representable in the register type (never round or clamp silently).

1. THE core SHALL ship a JSON Schema (`profiles/schema/buslink-profile.schema.json`) for profile schema v1 and Rust types for every field.
2. WHEN a profile is loaded, THE core SHALL validate it with the same rules as `tools/hooks/check_profile.py`: strict keys, duplicate JSON keys rejected, support levels `generic | documented | simulated | hardware_verified`, `source` required for documented/hardware-verified, passing hardware evidence required for `hardware_verified`, unit ID 0 never a default, word order explicit for multi-register types, write bounds inside `valid_range`, commands only on `simulated_only` profiles.

1. Every sample SHALL carry one quality: GOOD, TIMEOUT, CRC_ERROR, EXCEPTION(code), STALE, DECODE_ERROR or DISCONNECTED, plus `age_ms`, a receive timestamp and an optional source timestamp.
2. WHEN a read fails, THE core SHALL keep the last good value with its original timestamp, and its age SHALL keep growing; the failed sample SHALL NOT carry a fresh timestamp for that value or a substitute zero.

2. THE core SHALL provide a scripted `FakeTransport` driven by a manual clock so protocol and scheduler tests are deterministic and do not sleep.
3. THE core SHALL provide a Modbus TCP client transport over `std::net`.
4. THE core SHALL refuse to open a second worker for a link key that is already owned (one master per bus).

1. THE core SHALL run one worker per link that owns the transport; every read and write for that link SHALL go through its single queue.
2. THE worker SHALL serve commands before alarm reads and alarm reads before polling.
3. WHEN a command frame is executed, THE worker SHALL send it exactly once and SHALL NOT retry it, whatever the outcome.
4. WHEN the transport reports a lost link, THE worker SHALL mark every device on it DISCONNECTED, fail queued requests, and stop polling.

## Requirement 13: block merging (R5)

1. THE core SHALL merge registers of the same table into one read when they are contiguous (or within a configured maximum gap) and the block stays within 125 registers / 2000 bits, or a smaller device limit.
2. THE core SHALL never split one tag across two reads and SHALL never read an address that no tag covers unless the device's maximum gap explicitly allows it.

## Requirement 14: backoff and fairness (R4)

1. WHEN a device times out, THE core SHALL abort the rest of its cycle and back off exponentially (poll interval × 2ⁿ, capped, default cap 30 s); a successful cycle SHALL reset the backoff.
2. Reads MAY be retried a bounded number of times (default 1, only on timeout/CRC error, only when the device is not already in backoff). Writes are never retried.
3. WHILE one or more devices on a link are dead, every healthy device SHALL still be polled within `poll interval + Σ(other devices' blocks × (retries + 1) × timeout)`.
4. THE core SHALL count requests, GOOD results, timeouts, CRC errors, exceptions, decode errors, the last error and the achieved cycle time per device.

## Requirement 15: sample bus (D4)

1. THE core SHALL publish every sample on one broadcast bus so that UI, historian, LAN view and MQTT see identical values and qualities.
2. WHEN a subscriber lags behind, THE bus SHALL report the number of lost samples to that subscriber instead of dropping them silently.

## Requirement 16: command service (N1, R18, D8)

1. THE command service SHALL be the only code that builds FC05/06/15/16 PDUs.
2. THE command service SHALL follow `Idle → Armed → Previewed → Confirmed → Sent → ReadBack → Done | Failed`, with a single attempt per confirmation.
3. WHEN an operator arms a device, THE arming SHALL expire after 60 s idle (configurable) and SHALL be dropped on disconnect, reconnect, profile change or app background.
4. WHEN a command is previewed, THE service SHALL check, in order, arming, role, writability, bounds (`min`/`max`/`step`/`allowed_values`, reject never clamp), unit ID ≠ 0, and SHALL return a preview with device, unit ID, register doc address and PDU offset, old value, new value in engineering units, raw value and the encoded frame.
5. THE service SHALL send only after `confirm` with the ID of the current preview, and SHALL send at most once per confirmation.
6. AFTER sending, THE service SHALL read back and report verified, mismatch or unknown; a timed-out write SHALL be reported as effect unknown (read back, never retried).
7. Every transition SHALL append an audit record (time UTC, session, user, role, device, profile ID + version, function, address, old value, requested value, raw request, raw response or exception, read-back result); WHEN the audit record cannot be stored before sending, THE service SHALL NOT send.
8. Named profile commands SHALL only run on `simulated_only` profiles connected to a simulator link.
9. Acknowledgement and read-back SHALL be reported as separate fields (write acknowledged ≠ process reached target).

## Requirement 17: historian (R20, D9)

1. THE core SHALL store sessions, devices, tags, samples, events, command audit and outbox tables in SQLite (bundled) in WAL mode.
2. Non-GOOD samples SHALL be stored with their quality and a NULL value so that trends break at gaps.
3. THE command audit table SHALL be append-only (updates and deletes rejected by the database).
4. THE core SHALL insert samples in batches, apply a logging interval separate from the poll interval (quality changes always stored), and compute per-minute min/max/sum/count rollups from GOOD samples only.
5. Raw values SHALL be stored losslessly (registers as bytes, 64-bit integers exact).

1. THE core SHALL export CSV (UTF-8, ISO-8601 UTC, quality, exception code and age columns), XLSX (sheets Measurements, Devices, Configuration, Events, Commands; numbers as numbers) and JSON (64-bit integers as strings).
2. WHEN a text cell starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or carriage return, THE export SHALL prefix it with `'` in CSV and XLSX.
3. Every exported measurement SHALL include the profile ID and version.
4. Exports SHALL never contain secrets.
